title: 2027 1L Summer Associate
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
2027 Overview
Summer associates will be immersed in AbbVie’s in-house legal and compliance teams, learning about and handling real-world matters under the supervision of AbbVie attorneys and compliance officers. Summer associates will work with one of the following departments within the in-house legal or compliance team for the duration of the summer internship:
Patent Legal Academy
Work on a wide variety of patent prosecution and IP (patent, trade secret) litigation-related tasks, which may include drafting materials for U.S. and foreign patent prosecution, listing patents in the FDA’s Orange Book, analyzing freedom-to-operate issues, addressing contractual issues, evaluating issues related to biopharmaceutical patent and trade secret litigation, and participating in strategy meetings with in-house and outside prosecution and litigation counsel.
Clinical R&D Legal Academy
Work on a wide range of clinical trial-related legal and regulatory matters in support of AbbVie’s therapeutic pipeline. Provides support for AbbVie’s global clinical research-based pharmaceutical business, including: clinical trial design; executing transactions required to get a clinical trial up and running, conducting legal analysis relating to patient-related matters such as informed consent, recruitment and retention strategies, and integration of novel technologies into AbbVie’s clinical trials; and providing global regulatory advice relating to AbbVie’s pipeline programs.
Corporate Legal Academy
Work in key corporate legal areas such as corporate financing, securities compliance and disclosure, compensation and benefits, and corporate governance.
Strategic Transactions Academy
Substantive legal work related to acquisition transactions as well as new and existing collaborations; assessing antitrust risks associated with mergers, acquisitions, and licensing transactions; and venture capital transactions.
Global Commercial Legal Academy
Support comprehensive legal and strategic guidance to Marketing, Sales, Medical Affairs, and Regulatory Affairs teams. Advise on a broad range of matters involving the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Office of Inspector General (OIG), and other applicable laws, regulations, and industry guidance relevant to our business.t various pharmaceutical and aesthetics brands by partnering with attorneys to deliver
Operations, Privacy, and Technology Academy
Support the Operations function, which is responsible for AbbVie’s product manufacturing, procurement of goods and services, quality assurance, supply chain, and various aspects of product development; support the Legal Privacy team; and work on various Legal Technology projects, including those related to AI and the use of data across the enterprise.
Litigation/Employment/Compliance Academy
Work alongside attorneys across AbbVie’s Commercial Litigation, Employment, Labor & Immigration, and Legal Compliance teams.  Opportunity to work across a broad array of litigation and counseling matters, including areas such as product liability, antitrust, contractual disputes, visa and other immigration issues, and compliance with relevant laws including the Anti-Kickback Statute, Food, Drug & Cosmetic Act, Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, and many others.
Office of Ethics and Compliance Academy
Gain hands-on experience by supporting the Compliance team in activities such as conducting policy assessments, developing and supporting training initiatives, monitoring business practices and participating in investigations to help promote compliant conduct under healthcare and pharmaceutical industry codes, laws, and regulations. This role will also involve cross-functional collaboration with teams in Operations, Commercial Brands, R&D, Privacy, and International.
***
All summer associates will research and present on a legal or compliance issue related to their work and will have the opportunity to meet and work with AbbVie’s in-house and outside counsel and compliance professionals, including partnering closely with both a manager and mentor who will both provide ongoing guidance and professional development.
By the end of the summer, AbbVie 1L Summer Associates should have attained:
practical experience working for a global biopharmaceutical company in an interesting and evolving area of law,
an understanding of how in-house attorneys and compliance officers provide value to their company as trusted advisors to the business,
leadership opportunities and experience building business relationships effectively, and
meaningful writing and communication development.
How to Apply
Submit your application, which includes your resume and related information at the AbbVie Career Site AND Email a single PDF consisting of the documents set forth below to AbbVieLegalAcademy@abbvie.com.
Current resume
A letter explaining your interest in the AbbVie 1L Legal Academy Program, including your ranking of your top three choices among the internship programs listed above.
A personal statement addressing how this program will be career transformative and enable you to be a leader within the legal profession or greater community
Undergraduate transcript (unofficial)
If applicable, other graduate transcripts (unofficial)
In addition, as soon as your first semester law school grades are available, please email your unofficial law school transcript to  abbvielegalacademy@abbvie.com .
Preference will be given to applications received by January 11, 2027.
Qualifications

Must be enrolled in law school the semester following your internship
Strong undergraduate academic background, including in relevant disciplines

Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field
Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the internship
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Preferred Qualifications
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)
Proficient in computational modeling techniques (e.g., fluid dynamics, discrete element method)

2027 Formulation Sciences Internship Overview

Join AbbVie's Pharmaceutical Technology team within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) to support late-stage formulation development for a solid oral dosage form. This internship focuses on investigating excipient compatibility, specifically the interaction between common solid oral excipients and chemical stability. The intern will work alongside experienced formulation scientists and analytical chemists to characterize this phenomenon and help define strategies to ensure robust, high-quality drug product formulations. The intern will also present findings to department leadership and potentially contribute to an external conference poster or publication.

Investigate the mechanism of excipient degradation in the presence of pH modifiers using appropriate analytical techniques (e.g., HPLC, titration and colorimetrical methods).
Collaborate on LC/MS analysis to identify and characterize leachable degradants associated with the implications to stabilizing the drug substance in the formulation.
Evaluate degradation kinetics under varying temperature and relative humidity conditions.
Assess potential mitigation strategies, including formulation and process variables.
Summarize experimental results and present findings and recommendations to the project team and department.

Demonstrated ability to make decisions based on scientific data, to manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously, and to work with a sense of urgency.

Own and evolve the clinical process engineering capability within Clinical Development Operations, establishing the methodology, standards, and governance infrastructure that enable scalable, inspection-ready, and operationally excellent processes across the enterprise. AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
As a Study Feasibility Director, you will be part of AbbVie’s Clinical Development Operations (CDO) function, which is responsible for running clinical trial operations around the world.
In this role you will partner with and advise study teams on design feasibility and certain aspects of design strategy, including country and site selection, protocol review and assessment of patient burden, and related implications for patient recruitment and study timelines. This is a highly collaborative and analytical role, which will rely on your expert facilitation skills, your ability to influence without authority, and your strong experience in clinical study design, operations, and management.
Responsibilities:
Lead and develop Direct Reports: Managers and Associate Directors
Leads cross-functional clinical study team, Integrated Evidence Strategy Team and Asset Strategy Team interactions to assess overall design and operational feasibility
Conducts detailed scientific, analytical, and operational analyses to prepare for and support team engagements
Provides scientific and strategic consultation and recommendations on country strategy, site selection, protocol and patient burden, recruitment, and timelines
Leverages broad and deep scientific and organizational knowledge to work within and across therapeutic areas
Identifies risks from multiple perspectives and proposes potential mitigation strategies and solutions
Designs, prepares, and runs cross-functional meetings and forums to be effective and for clear outcomes
Identifies and analyzes important connections within and across therapeutic areas to optimize study performance at the portfolio level
Leads and manages cross-functional initiatives and organizational change workstreams
Design and develop study, program and portfolio level feasibility tools and processes
Improves and standardizes the clinical trial development process across the portfolio
Bachelor’s or advanced Degree, preferably in pure, applied, or technical sciences
Minimum of 10 years of pharmaceutical related experience, 8 years in clinical research/project leadership/consulting, 4 years in a managerial role
or Advanced degree (MBA, PharmD, PhD, or MD in a health care or related field) desirable with minimum of 2 years in clinical research/project leadership/consulting
Drug development and/or scientific project leadership experience preferred
Therapeutic area background in Oncology, Neurology, or Immunology preferred
Strong working knowledge of pharma drug development processes at a study, program, and portfolio level
Recognized leader in complex scientific analyses and decision making
Demonstrated leadership skills with broad scientific, strategic, and business orientations

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Communicates/presents key Clinical Pharmacology information/strategy to senior and executive management, regulatory agencies, and external peers. Supports strategic planning for drug development activities and projects to achieve departmental strategies, goals, and objectives. Utilizes scientific expertise to provide appropriate interpretation of data and relates implications of results to management. Serves as liaison to other departments/divisions for any study/project needs. Understands linkages across businesses and understands the impact of business decisions and solutions. May lead teams within Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacometrics and accountable for effective performance of the teams.
Responsibilities
Leads Clinical Pharmacology/PK/PD activities and multiple major projects. Assists R&D senior management in the selection of action plans that best meets drug development business objectives.
Identifies issues and help with issue resolution. Conducts risk assessments and assists in development of contingency plans. Assures project remains in alignment with strategic objectives.
Provides overall timelines to assess portfolio opportunities. Negotiates with other functional areas on project outcomes and deliverables to meet conflicting demands (time, cost, quality/performance).
Provides scientific and strategic consultation to R&D, Regulatory, and all levels of management on critical decisions and development plans.
Responsible for evaluating technical, scientific aspects of all AbbVie projects along with CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY management. Reviews clinical protocols and scientific reports for regulatory filings and anticipates regulatory questions. Leads CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY regulatory documents writing, submission and response to Regulatory agency comments.
Independently conducts due diligence assessments, summarizes results and represents CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY on business development teams.
Identifies and develops process improvement initiatives and reviews recommendations with management for approval and sponsorship.
Contribute to development of departmental goals. Influences strategic PK/PD decisions for the department.
Performs functions and responsibilities with the highest regard for quality and timeliness. Maintains up-to-date knowledge of PK/PD data analysis, modeling and simulation methods and software.
May manage personnel including development, mentoring, and effective delegation.
PhD with typically 7+ years of experience or Pharm D with typically 9+ years of experience in a relevant field, MS or equivalent education with typically 15+ years of experience; BS or equivalent education and typically 17+ years of experience; (*relevant field includes experience with PK, PBPK, PK-PD, Pharmacometrics or systems pharmacology, Drug metabolism/Transporters)
Excellent interpersonal skills
Knowledge and experience in multiple therapeutic and/or functional areas
Experience across range of development phases
Knowledge of AbbVie and Pharma drug development processes
Must have demonstrated leadership competencies in PK/PD, Biopharmaceutics, and Pharmacometric activities from planning, implementation through completion across multiple projects
Scientific project leadership or related experience
Project management skills such as scope management, progress tracking/driving as well as time management
Participates in initiatives and advancement of CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY

• Knows the business and the cross-functional contributions needed to deliver results
• Persistent and resilient finds the way to move good ideas forward

title: Director, Global Program Manager - Oncology
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Facilitates and drives cross-functional team effectiveness across the Asset Strategy Team by translating interconnected strategies into clear asset-level direction and execution within context of enterprise needs, disease area strategy, and therapeutic area objectives.
Proactively identify, communicate, and manage asset and disease level risks and subsequent mitigation plans. Ensure timely and accurate reporting within asset and/or disease area, including management of systems, and partnership with planning group in development of timelines.
Acts as the “COO” for the asset. Serves as the strategic thought partner to the ASL and Asset Strategy Team (AST) by synthesizing complex inputs across strategic cross-functional deliverables, and related strategies into aligned decisions and actions.
Serves as the strategic enabler of the Asset Team (AST), continuously driving value by optimizing team performance, streamlining cross-stakeholder communications, and developing compelling strategic narratives for governance forums.
Coaches and mentors Deliverable Team PM (DTPMs) and Project Planners to high performing project management expectations.
Responsibilities:
Drive and contribute to Asset Team strategy and execution. Serves as a core strategic partner to the Asset Strategy Team, coordinating activities and deliverables that translate interconnected strategies into executable plans. Bring critical thinking, business acumen, and enterprise perspective to cross-functional discussions, helping the team and the AST understand how their asset fits into the disease strategy bigger picture across the disease area. In partnership with the ASL and disease-area stakeholders, contribute to and influence cross-functional strategy across the portfolio.
Ensure strategies are translated into integrated evidence plans across sub-teams and governance forums , with clear accountability and follow-through.
Partner with Project Planners, and DTPMs and DST PMs to ensure timely, accurate, and strategy-linked timelines, milestones, and reporting, including tracking progress against AST goals. Use scenario analysis and analytics to support strategic decision-making, prioritization, and portfolio tradeoff discussions. Ensures dashboards, reports, and systems are timely and accurate.
Proactively identify, communicate, and manage asset timelines and risks with a stronger focus on strategic tradeoffs and early escalation. Partners with the ASL to identify and manage risks to the asset strategy, not only to individual deliverables. Apply judgment to assess implications of downstream changes to milestones, scenario plan, escalate critical issues appropriately, and ensure mitigation plans are in place for risks and transparent communication of cross-functional risks.
Drive cross-functional Asset Strategy Team alignment and effectiveness. Partners with the ASL to structure Asset Strategy Team discussions, improve decision-making, and ensure the team operates with focus, discipline, and efficiency. Coaches the team toward smaller, more focused strategy discussions and effective execution, ensuring the right SMEs are included in decision making discussions.
Prepare the AST for rigorous, strategy-focused governance reviews. Plays a central role in readying the Asset Team for more rigorous TASC reviews and governance interactions by ensuring strategy is clearly articulated, supporting materials are well-structured, and key messages are aligned to the appropriate audience level. Develops the strategic storyboard for governance interactions.
Strengthen execution excellence across the AST. Is the single “source of truth” across the asset for timelines, deliverables, budgets, and cross-functional connectivity across all DTPMs supporting the asset to ensure execution remains aligned to strategy and operating expectations. Ensures all reports, dashboards, and systems are timely and accurate.
Build team capability and consistency in project management practices. Coaches and mentors DTPMs to elevate and deliver consistent PM practices and seamless workstreams, ensuring alignment in execution standards, communication, and issue management across sub-teams.
Craft effective storylines and communications for stakeholders. Develops clear, strategic storylines that communicate the asset strategy, implications and downstream impacts of changes, and key decisions needed for governance and stakeholder engagement. Adjust messaging for different audiences to influence outcomes effectively.
Share best practices and support continuous improvement. Actively shares learning, benchmarks, and best practices with other GPMs, DTPMs, and Project Planners within the broader PM community to improve consistency, effectiveness, and strategic impact across supported assets.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a relevant scientific, business, or technical field
4-6+ years of experience in a variety of roles and associated teams in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry (research & development, commercial, project management, operations) with a record of expertise in one or more therapeutic areas
Minimum of 3 years supporting cross-functional teams in a core function (Program Management, Commercial, Development, Regulatory, Operations)
Demonstrated growth in strategic thinking, leadership, and strategic communication, with the ability to articulate strategy and downstream impacts clearly and effectively across multiple assets, stakeholders, and audiences
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to different levels and functions within the organization
Demonstrated knowledge of program management practices in the pharmaceutical industry
Preferred: Experience in late-stage drug development, including participation on a launch team
Experience with global teams in the pharmaceutical industry

Position Summary
The Director, SOX Lifecycle & Enablement owns the end-to-end SOX program lifecycle for the enterprise and serves as the senior deputy within the IC SOX Center of Excellence. The role directs the annual risk assessment and scoping process, the risk and control matrix, the Section 302/404 certification process, and enterprise deficiency management, and coordinates the network of Business Unit SOX Leads across the organization. The Director also directly manages the U.S. business unit advisory portfolio (Commercial, Operations, and the Accounting Center of Excellence), the program’s highest-complexity areas, operating as a player-coach.
The role is central to a multi-year modernization of the SOX program, including the transition of management testing to an internal Testing & Analytics Hub, expanded automation and continuous monitoring, and an AI-enabled controls platform. During this transition, the Director is expected to be hands-on: directly managing stakeholder relationships, deficiency evaluations, and external auditor positions while building the operating rhythm of a maturing program. SOX Lifecycle Ownership
Direct the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping process, including materiality-driven scoping decisions and coordination with the external auditor on scope alignment.

Oversee Workiva program administration (assessments, certifications, reporting) through the Senior Analyst, and partner with the AI & Analytics Enablement leader on platform direction.

Partner with the Testing & Analytics Hub, AI & Analytics Enablement, and IT SOX leaders to operate an integrated program.

10+ years of progressive experience in audit and internal controls, with significant SOX program leadership at a large public company or serving large public company clients.

Deep working knowledge of PCAOB AS 2201, the COSO 2013 framework, SEC Sections 302/404, and deficiency evaluation and aggregation practice.

The primary objective of this position is to lead the Finance team for US Skincare, comprised of SkinMedica, Diamond Glow and Latisse as well as upcoming pipeline assets. Position Summary
The Material & Capacity Planner is responsible for ensuring material availability and production capacity readiness to support the site's Master Production Schedule (MPS). This role evaluates material supply, capacity constraints, inventory health, and planning risks to ensure production commitments can be achieved. The position partners closely with Procurement, Manufacturing, Warehouse Operations, Finance, Quality, and Supply Chain Planning to identify risks early, drive mitigation activities, and support operational decision-making.

Material Planning & Readiness
Own material availability across all production plans and manufacturing schedules.
Review material requirements versus inventory, open purchase orders, and supplier commitments.

Maintain planning dashboards and readiness metrics.
Lead root cause analysis for recurring shortages and planning disruptions.
Provide proactive reporting of production red flags and risk indicators.

Collaborate with Warehouse Operations regarding inventory availability and material flow.

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Medical Affairs (MA) organization provides patients, healthcare providers and payers everywhere with the practical and clinically relevant information and solutions they need to use AbbVie products safely and effectively, throughout the product lifecycle and the patient’s journey.
Scientific Director provides medical and scientific input into strategic and operational medical affairs activities for AbbVie’s Neuroscience portfolio such as: health care professional and provider interactions (Payers, Patients, Prescribers, and Providers); generation of clinical and scientific data (enhancing therapeutic benefit and value); educational initiatives (medical education, data, guidelines, and value proposition); safeguarding patient safety (risk minimization activities and safety surveillance activities).
Works closely with commercial teams to provide strategic medical input into core brand (product) strategies, and to support medical and marketing activities (promotional material generation and product launches) and market access.  Executes core medical affair tactics to support launch. Collaborates with clinical development on Medical Affairs support of priority trials.
Key responsibilities:
Contributes to the development of brand strategies.
Lead and support Medical Affairs initiatives (strategy and tactics) for Parkinson’s Disease asset launch
Contributes to the development of and leads the execution of the Medical Education / Advisory Board & EE Engagement Plan generation in line with TA plan. Lead the individual (Global) Conference planning and execution.
Leads the development and execution of internal training activities
Generates clinical and scientific data per evidence gap assessment.
Responsible to manage budget for assigned projects.
May support cross-functional teams with subject matter expertise.
Actively contributes to the development of a TA EE Engagement Plan.
Contributes to the generation of MI communication content and supports training on Medical Information (MI) materials.
Responsible for performing the accurate and detailed medical review of complex advertising and promotional materials for assigned therapeutic area(s) within Medical Affairs. Provides timely and accurate reviews of promotional materials in accordance with established policies and practice standards, including regulatory guidelines to meet customer needs.
May assist as consultant and liaison with other corporations when working under licensing agreements and/or in the evaluation of new business development opportunities.
This is a hybrid role based in Lake County, IL preferably
Bachelor’s Degree in the sciences required. Advanced Degree PhD, PharmD, PA or NP preferred. Residency or additional post doctorate experience preferred.
5-7+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry or equivalent; substantial understanding of relevant therapeutic area required.
Knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory requirements governing clinical trials and experience in the design of protocols preferred.
Interactions normally require the ability to gain cooperation of others, conduct presentations of technical information concerning specific projects and schedules, etc.
Ability to interact externally and internally to support global business strategy. Must possess excellent oral and written communication skills.
Works with some supervision and guidance. Exercises judgment within well-defined practices and policies.
Ability to interact with and coordinate appropriate scientific and medical activities with internal stakeholders (i.e. commercial, clinical operations, discovery, statistics, regulatory, etc.) as they relate to on-going medical affairs projects.
Works with some supervision and guidance. Exercises judgment within well-defined practices and policies.

description:
About AbbVie

Targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNPs) represent a key new modality to enable effective delivery of mRNA. The tLNP chemistry, manufacturing, and control (CMC) team (TCT) is a newly formed group under Biologics CMC, Development Sciences, R&D. TCT focuses on process development for tLNPs, including mRNA process development, tLNP process development, and formulation development.
The tLNP Process Development team is seeking a highly motivated, talented, and innovative scientist with expertise in mRNA-LNP process development and an interest in laboratory automation. This team is responsible for the end-to-end manufacturing process from purified mRNA to purified tLNP bulk drug product, including encapsulating mRNA with lipid components to form LNPs, conjugating LNPs with a targeting moiety, and purifying the final tLNPs via tangential flow filtration (TFF).
The successful candidate will help advance fundamental understanding of tLNP unit operations, such as mRNA encapsulation, bioconjugation, and TFF, as well as scaling up lab processes into pre-clinical, clinical, and commercial scale manufacturing processes. The candidate will also apply automation expertise to integrate off-the-shelf and custom-built hardware, software, and data workflows into flexible experimental platforms that increase throughput, reproducibility, and process understanding.
The end goal for tLNP Process Development team is to deliver a robust manufacturing process at commercial scale. This includes science-based, hands-on approaches in the lab to optimize process parameters and understand the impact of process parameters on critical quality attributes. First-principle-based and statistical modeling will be applied where appropriate. Along the pharmaceutical development life cycle, the team will be responsible for successful production of non-GMP pre-clinical safety study supplies and GMP clinical study supplies from a manufacturing plant on site or at third party manufacturers. The team will also lead the tech transfer of commercial processes into a commercial facility. Additionally, the team reviews appropriate sections of Common Technical Document (CTD) for regulatory submissions.
Success in this role depends on close collaboration with the mRNA process development, drug product development, and analytical development, digital and automation partners, as well as cross-functional partners across Biologics CMC and Synthetic Molecule CMC. The work directly advances cutting-edge mRNA-based therapeutics.
Responsibilities
Independently design, execute and interpret critical experiments to understand unit operations such as mRNA encapsulation, bioconjugation, and tangential flow filtration, and scale up these unit operations to commercial manufacturing batch size.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory research or method development, requiring minimal direction from supervisor.
May initiate new areas of investigation that are scientifically meaningful, reliable, and can be incorporated directly into a research or development program.
Demonstrates high proficiency across a wide range of technologies relevant to tLNP process development.
Formulate conclusions and design follow-on experiments based on multidisciplinary data.
Primary author of publications, presentations, regulatory documents and/or primary inventor of patents.
Proactively develop and implement innovative automation solutions (custom and off-the-shelf equipment).
Apply AI tools for structured data capture, analysis, and predictive modeling.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, and GMP compliance.
Direct mentorship of others.
BS, MS, or PhD degree in Chemistry, Material Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or equivalent.
Senior Scientist I :  BS with 10+ years', MS with 8+ years', and PhD with 0+ years' industry experience.
Scientist II : BS with 7+ years', MS with 5+ years' industry experience.
Experience with LNP mixing technology in an academic lab, or industry experience with LNP drug product process development. For mRNA encapsulation, experience with systems such as impinging jet, coaxial jet, or multi-inlet vortex mixer is required.
Possess thorough theoretical and practical understanding of mRNA encapsulation.
Experience with bioconjugation is required.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to answer scientific questions.
Demonstrated ability to learn, understand, and master new experimental techniques.
Ability to multitask and work within timelines.
Demonstrated scientific writing skills and strong verbal communication skills.
Preferred Experience
Experience scaling up LNP processes to gram-scale mRNA or above.
Prior experience with automating existing experimental setups as well as new automation equipment and ecosystems, such as Ignition.

Develop advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence models that support healthcare affordability and copay intelligence initiatives.

Design scalable and maintainable machine learning workflows and pipelines.
Implement model monitoring, automated retraining, model governance, and performance management processes.
Support development of enterprise AI products that can be scaled across multiple business functions.
Ensure solutions adhere to organizational standards for quality, privacy, security, and compliance.
Collaboration & Leadership
Partner with business stakeholders to identify opportunities where AI and advanced analytics can drive measurable value.
Serve as a subject matter expert in data science, machine learning, and predictive analytics.
Present findings, recommendations, and technical concepts to senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
Communicate analytical trade-offs, limitations, and recommendations clearly to business, technical, and senior stakeholders.
Mentor junior data scientists and contribute to the growth of the broader analytics community.
Stay current on emerging technologies and industry trends in AI, machine learning, and healthcare analytics.

Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Economics, Operations Research, or a related quantitative discipline.

Experience using modern software development and version control practices.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to translate business challenges into data-driven solutions.
Demonstrated ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams.

title: Senior Scientist I - Bio CMC Purification Process Development
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Biologics CMC Development team at AbbVie in the Bay Area has a long and rich history of biologics development. Located in a state-of-the-art facility in South San Francisco, the team leverages its comprehensive end-to-end CMC capabilities to work collaboratively through all phases of CMC development with a primary focus on advancing complex biologic therapies, such as multi-specifics, and novel modalities, to human clinical studies and eventual licensure. This role is within a team of highly experienced scientists and managers who have directly enabled the development/IND submissions of 20+ novel biologics and successfully filed two BLAs.
As a member of the CMC Purification Development group, you will apply strong downstream process-development expertise to design robust, phase-appropriate drug substance purification processes for GMP production, clinical studies, and eventual licensure. You will own purification deliverables for assigned programs, help define drug substance development strategy as a functional lead on cross-functional CMC teams, and communicate data-driven recommendations, risks, and tradeoffs to key stakeholders.
This position is an onsite role in a lab-based function. To be successful candidates must enjoy and thrive in a fast-paced and highly collaborative lab environment with daily face-to-face cross-functional interactions between scientists.
Responsibilities
Develop, optimize, characterize, and scale up purification processes for monoclonal antibodies, multispecifics, antibody-like molecules, and other complex biologic candidates across early- and late-stage drug substance process development
Lead technology transfer to internal or external GMP manufacturing sites; author transfer packages, support facility fit and readiness, and provide technical troubleshooting during clinical manufacturing
Develop viral clearance strategy and oversee studies with contract laboratories, including protocol development, technical review, data interpretation, and report approval
Optimize purification platforms and deepen process understanding through mechanistic modeling, statistical design of experiments, data analytics, and targeted wet-lab studies
Conceive and evaluate novel, advanced bioprocess technologies that are in line with the group’s strategy
Maintain current scientific knowledge by critically reviewing peer-reviewed literature, regulatory guidance, patents, and emerging industry trends, and translate relevant advances into program strategy, experimental design, and platform development
Seize opportunities to pursue project relevant leads that are in line with the group’s strategy
Write technical publications, reports, presentations, and regulatory filings including publishing research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting work at scientific conferences
Work efficiently, collaboratively, and cross-functionally to meet project deliverables and timelines.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, and GxP compliance, where applicable
Mentor and train junior scientists
Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent education and typically 10+ years of experience, Master’s Degree or equivalent education and typically 8+ years of experience, PhD and 0+ years with relevant postdoctoral or industry experience (Education in Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, Chemistry, or a closely related field)
Demonstrated understanding of downstream bioprocess unit operations, including affinity, ion-exchange, and hydrophobic-interaction chromatography; depth and virus filtration; tangential-flow filtration; and formulation or bulk drug substance handling
Proven ability to work independently, effectively plan and execute work activities, and prioritize task completion to meet project deadlines in a fast-paced environment
Demonstrated depth of scientific knowledge in protein biochemistry, separation science, and/or bioprocess engineering, with the ability to critically evaluate scientific literature and apply relevant findings to hypothesis-driven experimental design, data interpretation, and technical decision-making
Able to organize, analyze, visualize, and interpret complex process and analytical data using tools such as JMP, Python, R, or comparable software
Must be forward-thinking and be able to lead and contribute to scientific/technical discussions and innovation
Able to independently learn, understand and execute novel, advanced scientific techniques
Must have excellent attention to detail and ability to keep detailed written records
Proven record of authoring publications, technical reports, regulatory documents, and/or presentations
Has strong communication skills including verbal, written, and scientific data presentation
Able to work collaboratively within and outside of the group
Preferred:
Hands-on experience developing purification processes for monoclonal antibodies, multispecifics, antibody-drug conjugates, or other antibody-like molecules at laboratory, pilot, and/or GMP scale
Experience developing scalable purification processes and applying quality-by-design principles, including identification of critical quality attributes and process parameters, is required
Proven experience in mechanistic modeling of downstream purification unit operations (e.g. GoSilico, CADET, gPROMS or similar framework) including chromatography separations and/or membrane separations
Proven experience in programming liquid-handling robots (like Tecan or Hamilton systems) and automated chromatography platforms (like ÄKTA) to execute high-throughput screening and purification studies.
Proficient in writing methods and operating AKTA chromatographic instruments (such as AKTA Avant, AKTA Pure, AKTA Pilot, AKTA Ready or similar)
Has a strong understanding of statistical analysis, such as standard deviation and analysis of variance
Familiarity with design of experiment (DoE) software, such as JMP
Has a strong understanding of analytical techniques, such as SEC, RP, SDS, icIEF, mass spectroscopy, and ELISA
Has previous regulatory filing experience (e.g. IND/IMPD)
Experience authoring process-development reports, technology-transfer protocols, process characterization summaries, and CMC sections supporting regulatory submissions
Demonstrated scientific aptitude through authorship of peer-reviewed publications

The role combines analytical capability, systems knowledge, problem-solving, and strong communication skills to support data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement.

Identify opportunities to improve system functionality, user experience, workflow efficiency, and data accuracy.
Support system integrations by documenting business requirements, investigating operational issues, and coordinating resolution with technical teams.
2. Operational Reporting, Analytics & Business Insights | 30%
Develop, generate, and maintain recurring and ad hoc operational reports using ServiceNow, Excel, and other available reporting tools.
Analyze ticket volumes, service-level performance, resolution trends, workflow effectiveness, system adoption, and operational performance.
Investigate recurring issues, process inefficiencies, and emerging trends to identify potential root causes.
Translate complex data into actionable business insights, identifying operational risks, improvement opportunities, and recommended actions.
Develop dashboards, visualizations, and executive-ready presentations that communicate performance results and their operational implications.
Summarize and present findings and recommendations to TA Operations, Operations & Innovation, and broader Talent Acquisition stakeholders.
Partner with Process Optimization and operational teams to evaluate improvement opportunities and measure outcomes.
Support workload forecasting, capacity analysis, and identification of emerging service-delivery trends.

Document current-state and future-state workflows, business rules, decision points, and functional requirements.
Partner with HRIT and Process Optimization to support automation design, implementation, testing, and validation.
Maintain a pipeline of identified workflow improvement and automation opportunities and provide recommendations on potential priorities.
Track and report the operational impact of implemented enhancements, including efficiency gains, reduced manual effort, and improved user experience.
4. Knowledge Management & AI Enablement | 15%
Support the ongoing maintenance, organization, and optimization of the ServiceNow knowledge management environment.
Maintain knowledge content standards, article metadata, categorization, and documentation accuracy.
Analyze operational trends and recurring inquiries to identify knowledge gaps and opportunities to strengthen self-service capabilities.
Partner with subject matter experts to develop and update standard operating procedures, system documentation, and knowledge articles.
Support AI-enabled service-delivery initiatives, including Now Assist and virtual assistant capabilities, through knowledge optimization and identification of potential use cases.
Monitor knowledge effectiveness, adoption, and recurring support needs and recommend improvements to support operational efficiency and self-service.

Support the standardization of Talent Acquisition system workflows, documentation, business rules, and operational controls.
Coordinate with HRIT, HR Operations, TA leadership, and technology partners to support consistent system execution.
Maintain system process documentation, workflow inventories, enhancement records, and change logs.

Support technology releases, change readiness, stakeholder communications, and adoption activities.

3+ years of experience in business operations, systems analysis, reporting and analytics, HR technology, process improvement, or related functions.
Experience generating reports, analyzing operational data, identifying trends, and developing business-focused recommendations.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, data manipulation, and trend analysis.
Experience working with enterprise systems, workflow platforms, or service-management technologies.
Experience documenting business requirements, workflows, and process improvements.
Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.
Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint with the ability to develop clear, compelling presentations for business stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain data findings and technical concepts to nontechnical audiences.
Ability to independently manage multiple priorities and assigned deliverables while collaborating effectively with cross-functional stakeholders.

Experience with ServiceNow HR Service Delivery (HRSD), including reporting, workflows, knowledge management, or enhancement coordination.
Experience with HR or Talent Acquisition technologies such as SmartRecruiters, Workday, or similar platforms.
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or comparable data-visualization tools.

title: Director of Engineering, Real Time Experience (RTX)
description:
The Opportunity
Adobe's Digital Video & Audio (DVA) business builds Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Media Encoder, the tools that filmmakers, broadcasters, and creators trust to tell their stories. At the center of these products sits the Realtime Experience (RTX) team. RTX owns the rendering engine, GPU abstraction layer, compositor, video player, importer and exporter host, and Effects and Transitions SDK. Every frame our customers play, edit, and export passes through this stack.
The next 12 months will define the future of video creation at Adobe. RTX is finishing its GPU-first pipeline, moving to a modern graphics API, and designing how AI-native rendering fits in. Leader for this team will shape the engine under Premiere Pro and After Effects for years to come.
We are hiring a Director of Engineering for RTX. The team is senior and highly specialized, and it needs a leader with matching depth. The Director will own these modernization efforts and align the many teams that touch rendering, as Topaz and LTX integrations arrive.
What You Will Do
This role sets the technical vision for the rendering technology behind DVA's desktop products, with a near-term focus on Premiere Pro performance and stability. Architectural decisions come with clear investment plans for engineering and quality engineering.
Deliver the GPU-first rendering pipeline to improve playback, scrubbing, and dropped frames.
Choose and lead the move to a modern graphics and compute API such as DirectX 12, Vulkan, or Dawn/WebGPU.
Define how AI features and partner technologies such as Topaz and LTX fit the render pipeline while keeping quality and user experience high.
Unify rendering, effects, and transitions across desktop, web, and mobile.
Build lasting partnerships with technology leaders and shape our roadmap around their platform plans.
Work with media and format teams to modernize legacy components, and align partner teams on shared priorities.
Lead the engineering side of a Developer Relations effort to unify and document our SDKs and raise third-party plugin quality, protecting a key competitive advantage.
The Director also grows a team of managers, architects, and senior engineers, protects the quality bar, and coaches leaders as the organization changes.
What We Are Looking For (Must Have)
Are you a technical leader whose judgment shapes the product? The ideal candidate does not need to write shaders, but knows which paths lead to great outcomes and can defend that view to engineers, partners, and executives.
12+ years of software engineering experience, with deep architectural judgment in GPU-accelerated, real-time rendering, graphics, or media systems.
5+ years leading engineering teams, with proven people leadership at senior engineering manager level or above, including developing managers and growing careers.
Experience building or leading performance-critical software such as rendering engines, playback and compositing systems, game engines, or broadcast tools.
Strong knowledge of GPU architecture and compute, and of modern graphics APIs including Metal, DirectX 12, Vulkan, and WebGPU.
A track record in large, mature C/C++ desktop codebases, modernizing them while continuing to ship.
A clear point of view on where rendering technology is heading, and the skill to turn it into a funded, staffed plan.
Strong influence across Product, Engineering, QE, and external partners.
Nice to Have
Understanding of video codecs, formats, and import and export pipelines, and how they affect playback and effects.
Experience in games, VFX, AR/VR, real-time 3D, or live broadcast production.
Experience adding AI or ML inference to rendering or media pipelines.
Experience unifying rendering across desktop, web, and mobile.
Experience building developer ecosystems, SDKs, or plugin programs.

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Difference You Will Make:
Our mission is to make every Airbnb engineer's day better by building world-class developer infrastructure that removes friction and provides the tools to unlock their best work. The Dev AI team specifically builds the foundational AI tooling and infrastructure that powers developer productivity across the entire software development lifecycle, also providing the building blocks for teams across the company to quickly and simply create their own domain-specific AI tools. We currently serve as both a platform team and an internal AI consultancy for partner teams building their own internally-facing AI-powered solutions.
In this role, you will help to shape and execute the technical direction of the team's infrastructure and products. You'll work across a range of exciting problem spaces, from agentic coding tools and asynchronous AI workflow platforms, to SDKs for rapid internal AI app development and AI-assisted code migration. At Airbnb, you won't just build AI tools; your work will shape how individuals across the company work every day. The tools you create will directly accelerate the pace of innovation across our entire product surface.
We're a collaborative, low-ego, and highly-visible team that values experimentation, learning, and shipping. We celebrate what works and learn quickly from what doesn't. Given the rapid evolution of AI, we strive to operate with startup-like agility, iterating swiftly to evaluate and incorporate the most recent AI technologies into our developer tooling. If you enjoy building, collaborating across teams, thrive when given high autonomy, and are motivated to make the lives of other developers easier and more enjoyable, we’d love to hear from you.

Help shape and drive our AI for Developers strategy, partnering with Staff and Sr. Staff engineers to assist them in aligning architecture trade-offs and product direction
Stay current on the rapidly evolving AI tooling landscape, and help the team balance innovation with incremental, measurable developer impact
Serve as a champion, expert, coach, and consultant to empower teams and leaders across the company to adopt and leverage new AI capabilities in their day to day workflows

2+ years of experience as a full-time manager

Prior experience building developer infrastructure, tooling, or platforms, ideally at scale and with tools, frameworks, or systems commonly used in the industry

title: Briefing Program Manager, AWS Executive Briefing Center
description:
The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Executive Briefing Program is seeking an experienced Briefing Program Manager to plan and deliver high-value executive briefings for customers at one of our Executive Briefing Centers. As a Briefing Program Manager, you are responsible for the overall success of onsite executive briefings. This includes managing planning timelines, stakeholder expectations and communications, executive engagement, and the successful execution of each briefing. You will work with internal sales stakeholders to provide consultation on the design of briefing engagements, working backwards from the customer's business objectives to develop bespoke agendas and experiences that solve specific customer challenges and advance adoption of AWS services. You will work closely with supporting briefing team members to plan and execute engagements that deepen customer relationships and accelerate cloud adoption. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who builds partnerships easily, has strong project management and analytical skills, and can manage multiple briefings at once. They communicate effectively with executive stakeholders and deliver independently on both tactical and program initiatives, while seeking direction on complex or ambiguous engagements. They are organized, comfortable applying established processes and guidelines, collaborative, and able to work backwards from the customer to make data-informed decisions.
Key job responsibilities
- Manage the end-to-end planning and delivery of executive briefings at a single Executive Briefing Center, serving as the primary point of contact throughout the briefing lifecycle.
- Work backwards from the customer's business objectives to develop briefing agendas and facilitate experiences that connect AWS executives, technical subject matter experts, and customers in outcome-based discussions.
- Partner with account teams and internal stakeholders to provide consultation during the briefing planning process and set clear expectations with internal and external stakeholders.
- Build and maintain relationships with account teams, speakers, and vendors to deliver a streamlined, high-quality experience.
- Apply established playbooks and timelines, and recommend improvements to existing processes and tools based on customer feedback and delivery experience.
- Use data and metrics to track delivery, measure briefing effectiveness, and surface insights that may inform broader program improvements.
- Manage briefing meetings including kick-offs, planning calls, and post-briefing debriefs.
- Begin to mentor briefing coordinators and newer team members by sharing knowledge and best practices.
Travel: less than 10% of time.
A day in the life

title: Energy Analytics, TPM, Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation
description:
The Energy Analytics, Technical Program Manager (TPM) will scale power monitoring, insight generation, and energy and carbon reduction initiatives across Amazon's North America fulfillment operations. In this hands-on technical role, you will deploy and generate analysis from power metering infrastructure and implement load flexibility and energy optimization roadmaps that deliver measurable cost savings and carbon reductions. This work directly supports Amazon's demand-side power requirements and Climate Pledge commitments.
You will operate as an individual contributor, owning the delivery of defined and ambiguous work-streams while partnering with engineering, controls, data, operations and deployment teams to implement changes. You will influence cross-functional partners without authority, primarily at the team and management level, using data to drive decisions. You will integrate and analyze power metering information, providing load forecasts and generating cost and energy savings opportunities. Utility rate structures, time of day, demand ratchets and power factor penalties will influence your strategies. Technical assets influenced can include material handling, robotics, powered industrial trucks, lighting, heating ventilation and air conditioning, plug loads, electrical metering and more. Developed projects will be scaled across hundreds of facilities across the network, producing energy, cost and carbon benefit.
Key job responsibilities
● Build and execute technical solutions for energy and carbon reduction from pilot, data collection, through scaled implementation and measurement & verification (M&V) of results.  Energy and load optimization via control systems is a technical requirement: energy-conservation/standby modes, variable speed applications, and equipment scheduling.
● Drive continuous monitoring and energy efficiency improvements with Amazon's energy consuming assets.  Integrate power metering into our data sets, and develop analytics to identify opportunities, assess trending consumption changes, and measure benefits of conservation efforts.
● Prepare written analysis of feasibility studies and recommendations for various energy monitoring and power flexibility strategies.  Own metering data quality programs, check readings for completeness, outliers, and flag actionable improvements, and reconcile against known loads to ensure trusted insight generation.
● Develop metrics, baselines, and roadmaps that translate technical work into quantified outcomes (energy savings, cost savings or utility tariff arbitrage, load forecast, reliability, carbon reduction).
● Define and own technical approach and cross-system architecture for data configuration, standards and mechanisms for scalability and enforcement of key energy savings mechanisms. Decide how to build and prove new approaches managing tradeoffs for necessary business needs, rather than executing a defined scope.
● Manage projects against plans and objectives to ensure commitments are met, delivering against our power and Climate Pledge goals.
● Deep diving (troubleshooting) and unblocking issues that are prohibiting teams from pursuing energy reduction initiatives.
● Work with critical stakeholders on developing mechanisms for design standard integration for launching facilities that incorporate energy optimization procedures from Day 1.
● Analyze and communicate the financial impact of projects and initiatives (payback, return on investment, net present value)
● Serve as a technical reviewer for peers and partner engineers — reviewing control logic, metering architecture, and design-standard changes, and improving them on technical merit
● Quantify and own value add of energy savings mechanisms and how they reduce equipment runtime and increases reliability and lifespan.
● Calculate and report energy, water and carbon savings using International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol methodologies.
● Manage multiple, complex projects simultaneously.
● Produce clear documentation, playbooks, and reporting that make work-streams repeatable.
A day in the life
You might spend the morning querying newly integrated power-metering data and validating it against the distribution-panel hierarchy — resolving a data-quality gap — then analyzing load profiles and build an energy-savings or peak-shaving model that quantifies the opportunity by equipment class. You then define network rollout suitability and prioritize these opportunities across sites. In the afternoon you develop control logic changes to implement an efficiency opportunity, propose updates to a design standard, or define a measurement method for implemented energy and cost savings to your stakeholders. You balance trade-offs between energy savings, technical complexity, equipment reliability, and cost — bringing well-reasoned recommendations and escalating the most ambiguous decisions for alignment.
About the team
The Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation (GESA) Energy team is dedicated to delivering energy efficiency, cost savings, and demand flexibility within Amazon's fulfillment network. We partner closely with design, controls, data, procurement, operations, field engineering, and deployment teams — as well as external vendors — to ensure our energy consumption is monitored and optimized. Our focus in the coming years is scaling our energy monitoring and analytics programs, expanding behavioral and retrofit programs, expanding load flexibility for power resilience and cost arbitrage benefit, and enhancing asset reliability and lifespan through efficient operation. If you are energized by large-scale technical challenges and want to make a tangible impact on energy use, this is the team for you.

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- Experience in SQL Server/MySQL, or experience in Redshift and experience in any Bigdata architecture
- Experience working with existing and emerging technologies related to building energy (i.e. power metering, conveyance, robotics, controls, HVAC, charging infrastructure)
Preferred qualifications: - Experience managing cross-functional programs and release schedules

title: Principal Product Manager, Shipping Express, Amazon Air Cargo
description:
You're a Principal Product Manager with deep experience in supply chain, transportation, or logistics product strategy within complex, rapidly scaling organizations. You've owned end-to-end product vision for a shipping, delivery, or transportation product at scale, and you have a track record of turning operational networks into differentiated, customer-facing products that customers love and adopt to. You excel where the problem spans network operations, product definition, commercial strategy, and customer experience — and you bring the strategic judgment to define the right long-term bets while delivering near-term value.
You have strong analytical skills and are comfortable diving deep into transit-time and cutoff economics, network flow and injection constraints, coverage and lane profitability, pricing structure, and competitive benchmarking to decide where product and network investment drives outsized revenue and share impact. You understand that this is not project management — this is setting direction for a shipping product that competes head-to-head with industry leading services and must earn every shipper's choice.
High judgment is expected at the Principal bar: defining the product promise and service bar customer-back (not operations-forward), making trade-offs between operational feasibility and customer delight, deciding when to build versus influence a platform or operations team's roadmap, and influencing across operations, network design, commercial, finance, and engineering teams without direct authority. You set strategy that other senior leaders and teams align to, you regularly engage with senior leadership to secure investment and drive high-stakes decisions, and you are relied on to be right a lot. You have a proven track record of building a transportation or delivery product that became a durable competitive advantage.
Key job responsibilities
Strategic Product Management — Define the executive-level vision for the Shipping Express 2-day product and translate it into actionable multi-year roadmaps aligned across operations, network design, product, commercial, and engineering. Define the product customer-back — product promise, cutoff times, guaranteed delivery windows, tracking/visibility SLAs, pickup experience, coverage footprint, service tiers, and pricing framework — benchmarked dimension by dimension against UPS 2nd Day Air and FedEx 2Day. Own end-to-end outcomes and business impact (shipper acquisition and retention, volume and share growth, delivery-performance SLAs, cost per shipment, and shipper satisfaction).
End-to-End Product Lifecycle & Quality Ownership — Own the full product cycle for Shipping Express and the quality of the product at every stage:
Vision — Set the long-term product vision and the "why now," grounded in customer need and competitive gap.
Requirements — Translate the vision into clear, prioritized product requirements that engineering and operations can build from.
Phased launch — Launch in deliberate phases (pilot → scale → expand), defining the entry and exit criteria for each phase rather than attempting a single big-bang release.
Measurement — Instrument the product and define the success metrics up front; measure actual performance against the product promise and the business case after each phase.
Quality improvement — Identify quality gaps from the data (service misses, exceptions, defects, failure modes) and drive the highest-impact improvements back into the product and network.
Product evolution — Continuously evolve the roadmap based on customer feedback, operational quality and cost, and P&L outcomes — deciding what to double down on, what to fix, and what to retire.
Cross-Team & Network Leadership — Lead product vision and execution across multi-org dependencies, driving alignment across network design, sort/injection operations, air gateway capacity, and middle-mile/last-mile execution. Translate hard operational constraints (pickup-to-injection timing, gateway cutoffs, sort-center flow) into a single recommended network path and a product customers can rely on. Eliminate fragmented ownership and missed handoffs across the shipping journey; own the build-vs-influence calls and ensure capabilities land in the right long-term home.
Operational Excellence & Scale — Design a product and the supporting network capabilities that scale with volume growth without proportional increases in manual exception handling. Use data to identify and eliminate the highest-impact friction points across the pickup-to-delivery experience and the lanes that drive cost and service risk. Build the governance and review mechanisms that keep cross-org investment aligned year over year.
A day in the life
Set the strategic direction for the Shipping Express product across teams — aligning operations, commercial, and engineering around a single customer-back product definition, not a stack of operational compromises.
Deep dive into data (transit-time and on-time performance, cutoff and injection constraints, lane profitability, competitive benchmarks, shipper feedback) to shape the roadmap and decide where to invest for maximum share and margin impact.
Run the product cycle end to end — move initiatives from vision to requirements to phased launch, then measure outcomes, surface quality gaps, and feed them back into the next iteration.
Partner with engineering and operations leaders to shape network and product design, ensuring the product scales with volume growth and holds its service promise.
Unblock cross-org dependencies before they become escalations; frame program narratives for senior leadership — connecting network and product progress to business outcomes.
Spend time with Ops teams and in the network to pressure-test whether the product performs for shippers in the real world.
What this takes
Someone who toggles between deep product and operational insight and strategic product leadership — owning the full product cycle from vision through launch, measurement, and continuous quality improvement — and turning a complex transportation network into a scalable, benchmark-beating 2-day shipping product that shippers choose.

title: Principal Program Manager, WHS Strategy, Workplace Health and Safety
description:
Amazon's Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) organization is responsible for safeguarding the health and wellbeing of more than 1.2 million operations employees across Amazon's global operations network. WHS advances safety performance through three pillars: people, programs, and technology. The organization builds a self-sustaining safety culture, prevents incidents through engineering and standardized operational practices, and applies artificial intelligence and computer vision to drive faster, proactive safety interventions at scale.
We are seeking a Principal Program Manager to lead the WHS Strategy team. This is a high-visibility leadership role at the intersection of enterprise strategy, executive communications, and operational safety performance. The leader in this position will serve as the primary owner of WHS's strategic planning cycle and will be accountable for the quality, coherence, and timeliness of the safety narrative presented to Amazon's most senior executives, including VP, SVP, and Board-level audiences.
This role requires a strategic leader who is effective under pressure, comfortable navigating organizational complexity, and capable of exercising sound judgment on matters with broad impact. The right candidate brings deep experience partnering directly with executive leadership, the ability to bring structure to ambiguous problems, and a consistent track record of delivering on high-stakes commitments. A core requirement is the ability to take complex, technical safety programs and communicate them with clarity and simplicity to audiences ranging from front-line operators to Board members. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills are not a differentiator for this role; they are a baseline requirement.
Key job responsibilities
This leader will own the end-to-end strategic planning lifecycle for WHS, including the development of 1 to 3 year strategic roadmaps, annual operating plans (OP1/OP2), and recurring executive reviews at monthly, quarterly, and annual cadences. Specific accountabilities include:
Collecting, synthesizing, and integrating strategic inputs from WHS teams across the organization, then drafting that content into a single, unified voice that reflects the WHS leader's perspective, ensuring consistent messaging, tone, and narrative alignment from document to document.
Authoring and managing the portfolio of WHS executive-level documents, ensuring analytical rigor, narrative precision, and strategic alignment across every deliverable that represents WHS to senior leadership.
Partnering with operations, engineering, and technology organizations across Amazon to integrate health and safety priorities into their strategic plans, influencing outcomes without direct authority.
Designing and governing the mechanisms through which safety data is reported to leadership, including ownership of data lock processes that ensure consistency and accuracy across all executive-facing materials.
Identifying opportunities to modernize how safety performance data is visualized, shared, and consumed by decision-makers at every level, raising the standard for insight-driven reporting.
Managing the enterprise planning calendar and orchestrating cross-functional inputs from a broad coalition of WHS field teams, central program teams, and operations stakeholders globally.
Translating complex operational programs, technical initiatives, and nuanced safety concepts into clear, concise, and accessible content for executive and non-specialist audiences.
A day in the life
You are a results-oriented leader with a genuine intellectual curiosity about what drives safety performance in complex operational environments. You combine strategic thinking with operational discipline: you can frame a multi-year vision and then build the mechanisms to bring it to life. You are comfortable being the person in the room who is expected to have the answer, and you hold yourself to that standard.
You bring a data-driven approach to every decision, an instinct for continuous improvement, and the organizational fluency to move work forward across teams that do not report to you. You are energized by ambiguity, not paralyzed by it. You communicate with clarity and economy, recognizing that at the executive level, every word carries weight. You are ready to own the strategic direction of safety for one of the world's largest employers and to ensure that direction is understood, aligned, and acted upon from the front line to the boardroom.
This is an in-office role requiring five days per week on-site. Travel is expected at 10 to 20 percent annually.
About the team
The WHS Strategy team functions as the connective tissue between WHS's technical and operational organizations and Amazon's executive leadership. The team builds and manages the mechanisms through which WHS compiles, creates, and refines the strategic planning and reporting documents that represent safety performance at the highest levels of the company. This is the program management group that owns the majority of WHS executive-level content and serves as the central authority for safety data and narrative consistency across Amazon.
The team operates as a trusted, high-credibility point of contact for a large global network of senior and executive stakeholders. The work is inherently cross-functional, requiring the ability to synthesize competing inputs, reconcile inconsistencies in data or direction, and produce a unified strategic view under tight timelines. The team's output directly shapes how Amazon's senior leaders understand and act on safety.

description:

• Coordinate with regulatory and safety stakeholders to ensure automation deployments comply with applicable standards (e.g., FAA regulations for UAV systems, robotics safety standards).

• You Earn Trust with cross-functional partners by communicating transparently, documenting decisions clearly, and delivering on commitments.

LOCATION AND TRAVEL

Sustaining Technology Engineering (STE), within GES Sustainability & Automation, keeps Amazon’s deployed automation and robotics technologies reliable, standardized, and continuously improving across the network. Our portfolio spans drones, mobile robots, autonomous vehicles, and camera/sensor-based inspection systems — all powered by computer vision and machine learning.
