title: Senior Manager, Protective Services
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is one of the world's most trusted on-demand logistics platforms. The Global Safety and Security team exists to keep it that way, protecting our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across all our markets. We manage risk and create value through agility, technology, and a people-first approach. Our DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt brands now span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees. Protective Services is the function accountable for the safety of the people we protect and the environments they live and work in, wherever they are.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Manager, Protective Services to lead protective operations, reporting to the Director, Protective Services. This is as much a build-and-execute mandate as a leadership one. You own the decisions that keep protection working, including how teams are staffed and assigned, how protection is set for a given person and situation, what we spend and which vendors we use, what people are trained to do, and how incidents get handled.
This is a player-coach role, and the coaching half does not keep you off the field. You will work advances, travel with the people we protect, and take your turn in the rotation while setting the standard the team works to. Protection here is a service. It works when the people we protect can move through their lives with as little friction as we can manage, and when they trust the team enough to tell us what we need to know.
You own protective operations, training and standards, vendor management, incident response, and converged physical-cyber protection. Protective teams, intelligence, and cybersecurity work on the same problem simultaneously, and detection and intelligence capabilities drive our protective posture.
Success in the first year means a tight operating rhythm, training and qualification standards that hold up against the best protective programs, a team that is current and deployable on short notice, and protective decisions driven by intelligence rather than reaction.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead protective operations. Own staffing, assignment, protective decisions, resourcing, and response across the full scope of the program. Lead from within the work rather than from above it, and be accountable for how it performs.
Own training and standards. Set what people are trained on, qualified in, and expected to keep current, then verify it is happening and hold the records that prove it. Build a team that deploys on short notice and stays that way.
Own vendor and supplier management. Decide what we need and from whom, run competitive procurement, and set approval thresholds. Where a supplier is part of how we protect someone, they meet our standard.
Own incident response. Be the escalation point for protective events within your authority and make real-time calls on protection and resourcing. Escalate immediately on legal exposure, law enforcement involvement, or risk that reaches other teams, and write down what was decided and why.
Lead converged physical-cyber protection. Work with Protective Intelligence and Cyber Protective Services to read threat indicators and judge what testing and assessment findings actually mean. When a threat starts online, you decide how protection answers it.
Earn trust and keep friction low. Build relationships with the people we protect, their families, and their teams to make protection something they rely on rather than tolerate. Design the friction out, so we ask less of them for the same result.
We are excited about you because you bring…
Leadership and operating experience. Ten or more years in protective, security, or military operations, including five or more years managing people with hands-on responsibility for protective operations. You have held real decision authority, not advised someone who held it, and you are still close enough to the work to run it yourself.
Judgment under pressure. You make sound calls with incomplete information in fast-moving, high-consequence situations, and the record of those decisions holds up under later review.
Building, not inheriting. A track record of building or scaling protective capability and setting the standards, qualifications, and procedures other leads work to.
Breadth of scope. Experience running more than one protective discipline or program at the same time, including through other leads, accountable for cost, method, and staffing across all of it.
Technical fluency across physical and cyber security. You do not need to be a security engineer, but you need to think like one. You understand how networked systems are put together and how someone would go about taking them apart, you are comfortable with network security concepts, access control, surveillance, and residential security technology at the operational level, and you can tell whether a proposed fix actually closes the gap it claims to.
Service orientation and discretion. You have earned the confidence of the people you protect and the people close to them, and you have kept it. You handle sensitive information about who is protected, how, and where without exception.
Working well across teams. A record of partnering with intelligence, cybersecurity, legal, and business teams on matters that go beyond your authority.
Availability. Willingness to travel around 35 percent, with peaks near 50 percent, often on short notice, and to pick up the phone on protective events and serious escalations outside working hours.
Physical readiness for the work. The ability to stay on your feet and moving for long stretches across offices, residences, venues, and transit, to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds, to assist or move a person to safety, to work in tight spaces and sit in vehicles and aircraft for extended periods, to see and assess people, vehicles, and conditions at distance and in poor light, to communicate clearly in loud environments, and to drive in heavy traffic and bad conditions.
Endurance for the conditions. The ability to work outdoors and in transit in extreme heat, extreme cold, inclement weather, and crowds for as long as the work takes, to work irregular and long hours including nights, weekends, and holidays on short or broken sleep and across time zones, and to keep making good decisions while doing it.
Education. Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

location: San Francisco, CA; Sunnyvale, CA; Seattle, WA; New York City, NY
description:
About the Team
The Reliability Platform team develops the systems that empower engineering groups across all of our brands to own the reliability of their services without needing to become reliability experts.  Our offerings enable engineers to define and measure service level objectives (SLOs), surface insights to expedite investigations and drive incidents from declaration through root-cause analysis (RCA) and postmortem. When problems are detected earlier, mitigated faster and followed up on rigorously, our engineers can ship rapidly with confidence and we can collectively ensure that the consumers, merchants and Dashers that depend on DoorDash have the best possible experience.
Reliability Platform’s long-term vision is to operationalize a flywheel of reliability data and insights in order to continually raise the bar for our global engineering organization.
About the Role
As a Software Engineer on the Reliability Platform team, you’ll help design, build, and operate software and infrastructure that deliver on the team’s mission and vision described above in collaboration with expert peers across the Infrastructure and Product organizations. You will work on mission-critical back-end services and pipelines, complex orchestration workflows, self-service platform capabilities and agentic intelligence.
We see and believe in the promise of agentic AI to radically reshape and supercharge how we serve our users and stakeholders while remaining pragmatic and committed to delivering positive business-value outcomes as the ultimate goal.
Some examples of what the Reliability Platform team does:
Own and drive unification of incident management process and tooling globally across all DoorDash-owned brands
Create the framework that measures SLO compliance and quality across tens of thousands of endpoints and derive the programmatic insights that ensure engineering teams are informed and accountable for the quality of their products
Build the internal SRE Agent used in incidents which supports team/domain-specific knowledge bases and obviates legacy runbooks
Set up MCP for agentic use of Reliability Platform data + tools and enable other Core Infra teams to follow suit
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Deliver Innovative Capabilities: You don’t want to ‘turn the crank’ somewhere, but you want to contribute to strategic thinking and help us drive meaningful continuous improvement.
Be Customer Obsessed: We want to learn from our internal customers to ensure we are solving the right challenges, and also share our perspective to influence in areas of expertise
Hold a High Quality Bar: We need to lead by example in how we develop, build, test and ship our products to show that we can work at high velocity without sacrificing quality outcomes.
Automate Everything: Your first instinct is to ask how toil can be obviated or, failing that, automated away from humans.
Shape the Future of Operations: Experiment with agentic AI workflows that can propose, validate, and safely execute production changes — moving DoorDash toward proactive, self-healing systems in step with industry first movers.
We’re excited about you because you have…
Platform Engineering Mindset: You think in terms of APIs, abstractions, and workflows — you enjoy building systems that other engineers depend on every day.
Proven Experience: You have 2+ years of experience in an infrastructure, platform, or backend engineering role, showing you can deliver and maintain complex systems.

AI Alignment: You embrace the use of AI tools to be a more productive and capable engineer. This applies to coding, planning, supporting peers, and everything you do.

description:

Senior Data Engineer - Schaumburg
MISUMI | Data Platform
Own the data platform that MISUMI runs on
MISUMI is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to be the go-to owner of our Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. You will be the primary data engineer, with real ownership and real influence: the models you build and the pipelines you run are what Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support rely on to make decisions every day.
You will work hands-on with a modern stack (Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Git/GitHub) and with AI coding agents in your daily engineering work. You will also have the autonomy to take requests from intake to production, propose what we should build next, and shape safe team practices for agentic development. If you want a role where your judgment directly determines whether the business can trust its data, this is it.
Impact in this Role
The Senior Data Engineer is the go-to owner of MISUMI’s Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. This person turns data from business and production systems into trusted, analytics-ready models that Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support use to make decisions. Because this is the primary data engineering role, the accuracy, security, and reliability of the data platform, including regulated data such as CUI, depend on this person’s judgment and execution.
Essential Functions
Administer Snowflake: manage users, roles, grants, warehouses, resource monitors and security policies, and keep the environment secure, fast and cost-efficient.
Design, build, and own dbt models (staging, intermediate, marts, and the semantic layer) that turn replicated source data into trusted, analytics-ready tables with tests and documentation.
Build, operate, and monitor ELT pipelines from production and business systems into Snowflake, using Fivetran and related tools. Resolve connector failures, schema changes, backfills, and data-quality issues.
Act as the team’s primary technical resource for modeling and pipeline work. Take requests from intake to production independently, including scoping, estimating, and reporting status.
Translate business requirements into technical requirements and data models, and bridge the gap between business teams and technology. Ask clarifying questions, agree on metric definitions and acceptance criteria with stakeholders, and turn them into specifications the team can build and test.
Proactively identify opportunities where data, modeling, or automation can help the business get closer to its goals, and propose and prioritize them with stakeholders instead of waiting for requests.
Run an impact analysis before changing, deprecating, or removing any shared table, model, or connector. Use dbt lineage, Snowflake dependency and access metadata, and stakeholder review, and document a rollback plan.
Own the Git and GitHub workflow for the dbt project: branching standards, pull-request review, automated tests, and deployment.
Use AI assistants and agentic workflows in daily engineering work to speed up SQL and dbt development, testing, documentation, code review, and debugging, and help set safe team practices for using them.
Find the root cause of data-quality, performance, and pipeline problems and fix them at the source.
Tune queries, models, and warehouse usage, and advise engineers and analysts on efficient query patterns and table design.
Maintain data dictionaries, data-flow diagrams, and schema documentation.
Lead data design sessions and technical reviews, and explain design trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate new Snowflake and dbt features and tools, and recommend improvements to the data platform.
Mentor analysts and engineers on SQL and dbt best practices.
Work with remote, cross-functional teams across time zones.
Maintain and contribute to the Quality Management System (QMS).
Desired Traits
Five core skills. Candidates must show direct, hands-on production experience in each:
Snowflake administration and engineering: access control, warehouse sizing and cost control, query tuning, clustering, security controls, cloning, time travel, and data sharing.
dbt expert modeling: layered models, dimensional modeling, incremental models, snapshots, macros, tests, documentation, and CI/CD through Git.
Advanced SQL: CTEs, window functions, recursive queries, semi-structured data, and query tuning.
ETL/ELT tooling: Fivetran (our tool) or similar, including connector setup, schema drift, deleted records, backfills, and cost.
Agentic coding and development: daily use of AI coding agents that work in the repository and terminal (not chat-only use), with disciplined verification of everything they produce.
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of experience as a data engineer, designing, building, and operating data pipelines and warehouses.
6+ years of hands-on Snowflake experience in production, including administration: access control, warehouse management, and cost and performance monitoring.
5+ years building and maintaining production dbt projects (dbt Core or dbt Cloud), including testing, documentation, incremental models, macros, and CI/CD.
5+ years working with ETL/ELT tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Stitch, Matillion, Informatica, or Talend, plus experience with pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience using agentic coding tools that work directly in the codebase (not chat-only AI use) in daily data engineering work. This includes building agentic workflows or tool integrations for data work, such as MCP servers, custom agents, or automated dbt and pipeline checks, with concrete examples of the workflows and results.
Expert SQL, including CTEs, window functions, and performance tuning.
Daily use of Git and GitHub pull-request workflows.
Experience being the primary or sole owner of a data platform, or the technical lead for one.
Experience administering data platforms that hold regulated data (such as CUI under NIST SP 800-171), including access control, audit logging, encryption, and data classification. Must be able to pass a background check and complete required CUI and security training.
Preferred
Direct Fivetran experience, including connector management.
Experience with Sigma Computing, or with Tableau, Looker, or a similar BI tool.
Experience modeling ERP and CRM data, such as NetSuite or Salesforce.
Python for data tooling and automation.
Snowflake SnowPro certification or dbt certification.
Infrastructure-as-code experience for Snowflake, such as Terraform.
Background in manufacturing, supply chain, or marketplace businesses.
Abilities
Write advanced SQL on large, complex datasets, including semi-structured data such as JSON in Snowflake VARIANT columns.
Apply data warehousing and dimensional modeling principles to turn business requirements into well-structured, maintainable models.
Work independently: take an open-ended problem, define the approach, deliver it, and raise risks early instead of stalling.
Use sound production judgment: verify before changing shared systems, plan for failure, and know how to roll back.
Use AI tools with discipline: give clear context and constraints, review and test every AI-generated change, and stay accountable for the result.
Solve hard problems methodically: break an unclear problem into testable hypotheses, gather evidence from logs, lineage, and query history, confirm the cause before changing anything, and verify the fix worked.
Communicate clearly in writing and in person, giving business context to engineers and technical context to non-engineers.
Physical Demands
The employee routinely sits, talks, hears, and uses hands and fingers to operate a keyboard. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Travel
Ability to travel 5% annually in the US for team meetings, offsites, and conferences.
Ready to own the platform?
If you have run production Snowflake, dbt, and ELT at scale, you work daily with agentic coding tools, and you want to be the person the business trusts with its data, we would like to hear from you. Apply today.

401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs

title: Electromechanical Technician
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
Performs all related duties necessary for maintenance and repair of machinery and equipment used in production plant; for maintenance and repair of the physical structure, electrical, and plumbing systems of the buildings; and, when necessary, performs various construction/remodeling duties to company property as assigned.  Also performs electrical maintenance and repairs of plant production equipment and commercial building.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follows all company safety rules and policies.
Must be able to maintain 5S program standards including organizing, labeling, cleaning and sustaining of workstations, toolboxes, work areas and parts shelving and cabinets.
Must be able to read, understands and follows schematics, wire and parts diagrams, sketches, operation manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to repair and maintain machinery and mechanical equipment such as, but not limited to, motors, pneumatic, hydraulic, conveyor systems and production machines and equipment using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing instruments.
Observes mechanical devices in operation and listens to their sounds to locate causes of trouble. Root Cause
Dismantles machines or equipment to gain access to and remove defective parts, replaces defective parts and motors, and adjusts feed mechanisms.  Replaces or repairs machine belts.  Performs these duties with the aid of such equipment as hoists, cranes, hand tools and power tools.
Holds scaffolding members in place or tightens bolts to erect working platforms about machines.
Cleans and lubricates machine parts, such as, but not limited to, shafts, pulleys, gears, and bearings, using rags, brushes, grease gun, oil can, and other required tools not specifically listed here.
Removes dust, dirt, grease and waste material from machines.
Painting machines or equipment to prevent corrosion.
May install and repair electrical systems and electrical and electronic components of industrial machinery and equipment, following electrical code, manuals, schematic diagrams, blueprints and other specifications, using hand tools, power tools and electrical and electronic test equipment.
Observes functioning of installed equipment or system to detect hazards and need for adjustments, relocation or replacement.
May diagnose/troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment, such as control circuits, motors and lighting fixtures, HVAC systems, using testing equipment, and make necessary repairs, such as replacing damaged or broken wires and cables. Troubleshoot to component levels
Tests malfunctioning machinery, using test equipment and discusses malfunction with other maintenance employees to diagnose malfunction.  Replaces faulty electrical components of machinery, such as wiring, fuses, relays, switches, electric motor bearings and motors and positions sensing devices.
May diagnose and repair or replace faulty electronic components, such as circuit boards, and mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic components of machines and equipment.
Maintains tools and equipment and keeps supplies and parts in order.
May repair electronic equipment such as industrial controls, audio systems, transmitters, and servomechanisms, following blueprints and manufacturers’ specifications and using hand tools and test instruments.
Converses with machinery/equipment operators to ascertain problems with machinery/equipment before breakdown and to determine if breakdown is due to human error or mechanical/electrical problems.
Tests faulty machinery/equipment and applies knowledge of functional operation of electronic/electrical systems or units to diagnose cause of malfunction.
Tests electronic components and circuits to locate defects, using oscilloscopes, signal generators, ammeters and voltmeters. Replaces defective components and wiring and adjusts mechanical parts, using hand tools and soldering iron.  Aligns, adjusts and calibrates equipment according to specifications.
Maintains records of repairs, calibrations and tests.
May connect wiring to lighting fixtures and power equipment, using hand tools.  May install control and distribution components such as switches, relays and circuit-breaker panels, fastening in place with screws or bolts, using hand tools and power tools.
May connect power cables to equipment and installs grounding leads.
Tests continuity of circuit to ensure electrical compatibility and safety of components using testing instruments, such as ohmmeter, battery and buzzer and oscilloscope.
May bend and cut conduit and wire, and drill holes in walls, floors and ceilings for electrical connections.
May connect wire to motors, fixtures, and other electrical equipment, replace switches and fuses and splice wire and insulates wire with friction tape.
May bend, cut and thread pipe, cut openings in walls, ceilings and floors for pipes, seal pipe joints with sealing compound.
May cut out and join parts for worktables, benches, shelves and other furnishings, using power tools and hand tools.
May be required to assist with plumbing repair work, building construction/remodeling/repairs, general machinery maintenance or repair duties.
May patch or replace plaster or plaster board and paint walls, ceilings, and trim of building.
May drill and break up concrete.
May mix and pour concrete for foundations.
May weld and fabricate a variety of deigns, including fixtures, carts, tables, and platforms using MIG, TIG and/or stick methods.
Clears clogged drains and replaces plumbing fixtures.
Inspects products and processes while performing job duties to ensure all work done meets or exceeds standards of the company’s quality program.
Works cooperatively and congenially with co-workers to achieve cohesive and productive work processes and work environment.
May provide ground watch for other maintenance employees using aerial equipment
May be required to assist with spill response clean-up
May be required to train other maintenance employees
Performs additional tasks as assigned by management or as the situation requires.
QUALIFICATIONS
Valid Texas Driver’s License required
3 + years’ experience in general mechanical maintenance of production machinery to include reading blueprints, wire diagrams, pneumatics, hydraulics, welding, root cause analysis, and requesting machine parts.
Possess minimum knowledge of electrical wiring repairs and installation, AC/DC controls, blueprints, schematic diagrams, pneumatics, and hydraulics.
Technical degree and/or license relating to electrical, mechanical or HVAC/Refrigeration - minimum of one preferred OR 40 hours of documented electrical training. License number and/or documentation must be provided before hire date.
Must be able to meet all minimum training requirements within first 6-12 months of hire date.
Obtain and Maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for powered equipment, including but not limited to, forklifts, scissor lifts, aerial booms, stock chasers, and floor scrubbers within first 90 days of hire date.
Capable of operating aerial lift equipment
Obtain and maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for power equipment.
Ability to follow verbal and written instructions regarding procedures required for various machine repair.
Ability to read and follow repair or installation instructions
Ability to use a variety of small hand tools, power tools, scissors lifts, and material handling equipment.
Possess basic mechanical aptitude and ability.
Ability to communicate clearly with co-workers (bi-lingual English-Spanish a plus)
Ability to read and follow written English instructions and complete PMs and work orders within Maintenance CMMS software. Some ability to write English responses.
Ability to understand basic online safety and cyber security courses presented in English and demonstrate understanding through multiple choice exam score
Ability to communicate through email
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
Attend work regularly and report promptly for duty on the days and at the times scheduled by the supervisor.
Schedule changes occur and should be handled in a productive manner
Working temperatures vary with seasonal changes where climate control is limited.  The environment is one in which noise exists.
Work occasionally outdoors in temperatures ranging from hot to cold and exposed to rain and wind
Sit on a forklift, stand, walk, squat, climb, or crawl for a combined minimum of eight (8) to ten (10) hours per day on a concrete surface.
Lift and carry components, tools, or other items weighing more than 35 pounds.  Any item over 35 pounds, is to be done with assistance
Pull and push up to 100 pounds.
Ability to work around hazardous chemicals.
Carries tools and equipment to and from storage and work areas.
May perform combination of physical movements to reach areas difficult to access including bending, stooping, squatting, reaching, twisting and rotation motions using head/neck, arms, wrists, waist, knees and arms while performing duties.
Handle small hand tools and power tools.  Handling may be done unilaterally (one-handed) or bilaterally (two-handed) depending on size and shape of object and task being performed.
Need corrected vision to be aware of surroundings and location of items needed and perform various other job duties.
Need corrected hearing to identify conditions in the environment (i.e. forklift horns, fire alarms).
Need mental alertness to identify, avoid, or resolve safety hazards.
Ability to work at elevated heights.
Ability to communicate with supervisors and co-workers.
Ability to wear designated personal protective equipment for the work assignment (i.e. safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, harnesses, hard hats, safety shoes)
Hours of Work
Monday – Friday, 6:00am – 2:30pm and OT when required including, but not limited to, frequent Saturdays with a schedule of 5:00am – 1:30pm

This is a unique, HQ-based Field Service Engineer role for someone who thrives on variety over a fixed territory. Day to day, the work is hands-on: installing, maintaining, calibrating, and troubleshooting complex servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems at customer sites. Training on MTS-specific technology is provided, and strong hands-on technical aptitude is essential.
Travel: This role involves frequent travel from home base in Eden Prairie, MN to customer sites across North America, since coverage assignments follow wherever a training or mentoring event or overflow need arises. Integrity
We operate with complete integrity and the highest ethical standards in all our interactions and dealings with our ITW colleagues, customers, suppliers, and stakeholders.
No compromises, no short cuts, and no exceptions.
There is no situation in which it is acceptable to compromise our integrity in order to improve business performance.
Our reputation and credibility are among our most important business assets.  We will not undertake or tolerate any behaviors that have the potential to do harm to either.
Simplicity
80/20 is not just something we do; it’s how we think.  It is our core philosophy and drives simplicity into everything we do by focusing on the “20” of any opportunity or problem that drives the “80” of the results or outcomes.
We recognize that complexity is a major performance inhibitor, and we are aggressive in working to minimize complexity in our business processes, structures, and systems in an ongoing and continuous manner.
Our ability to combine the advantage of large company resources with small company speed, responsiveness and flexibility is an important and distinct competitive advantage for ITW.  As a result, we will be proactive and intentional in minimizing non-value-added and bureaucracy across the company.
Trust
We trust that all ITW colleagues will operate with their best efforts and in the best interests of the company at all times.
At ITW, trust is assumed and not something that needs to be proven first.  As a result, it is essential that all of us consistently demonstrate trustworthiness in all of our behaviors and business interactions.
Trust is a critical enabler of our decentralized entrepreneurial culture.
Respect
We treat everyone as we expect to be treated and value the diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences of all our ITW colleagues at all levels of the organization.
We believe that only by having an inclusive culture and creating an environment where diverse opinions and perspectives are actively sought and freely shared can we be the best ITW that we can be.
The best way to ensure that we get the best ideas is to engage the broadest possible relevant group of employee stakeholders around a particular problem or issue.
It’s the quality of ideas that matter, not the power of position or authority.
Shared Risk
We recognize that continuously evolving and innovating is essential to ITW’s ability to remain a strong, successful and growing company, and that failures and mistakes are an essential part of the process.  We believe that if we are not making mistakes, we are not striving hard enough to improve and develop as individuals or as a company.
Once we decide on a course of action, we all take ownership and share the responsibility for the outcome, good or bad.  We share our successes and take responsibility for our mistakes and challenges as a team.
We focus on “solving the problem,” not “pointing the finger”.
Safety Vision
A workplace with Zero Safety Accidents, enabled by shared ownership of a proactive, continuous improvement mindset that reduces unsafe behaviors.
Quality
To establish, maintain and continuously improve internal processes and controls of our quality management system to meet regulatory requirements and to provide products of the highest quality that meet our customers’ needs and exceed their expectations.

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About Intuitive Surgical
Intuitive Surgical is a global leader in minimally invasive care and innovative surgical robotics. We advance the boundaries of medical care by continually fostering an environment rich in discovery, problem-solving, and growth. Our mission is to drive better, safer outcomes for patients, care teams, and hospitals, while cultivating a culture where professionals are empowered and inspired.
Role Summary
We are seeking an exceptional Assistant General Counsel, Intellectual Property, with deep expertise in patent portfolio management, IP-related transactions, and IP counseling.
This role offers the chance to work at the intersection of some of the most exciting technologies in robotics and medtech today: robotic assisted surgery, AI, computer vision, advanced instrumentation, imaging, and digital surgery. As an in-house IP attorney, you would partner directly with world-class engineers, scientists, physicians, and business leaders to help develop IP strategy for technologies that have the potential to improve patient outcomes and transform how surgery is performed around the world.
Intuitive is entering an exciting period of growth as we continue to expand our platforms, integrate AI and digital technologies, and push the boundaries of what is possible in minimally invasive care. If you enjoy working on breakthrough technology, working closely with innovators, and seeing your work directly influence the trajectory of a business and an industry, we invite you to apply to join our dynamic team.
Primary Function of Position
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will lead and manage an active patent portfolio, including management of patent application preparation, patent prosecution, and IP strategic development to identify and protect Intuitive’s valuable innovations.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will support a wide variety of IP-related transactional matters, including NDAs and other agreements covering collaboration, product development, and suppliers.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will support strategic deals and investments, such as M&A and licensing, including conducting IP-related due diligence, crafting and negotiating deal agreements, and advising on IP-related deal strategies.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will provide additional comprehensive IP-related legal support, including: litigation support (as needed), trademark protection, and trade secret protection.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP l will engage directly with engineers, scientists, management, clinical specialists, and executives, to translate technology developments into strong IP protection and support key business objectives.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP should become informed on industry trends and provide advice about industry and regulatory developments as well as development and implementation of operational and risk management processes and procedures.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will report to the Associate General Counsel, IP Strategy, and must escalate issues, as appropriate, and partner with all legal team members.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP must represent Intuitive Surgical with external parties with professionalism and strategic insight, including customers, regulators, affiliates, and industry trade groups
Job/Skill Requirements
Minimum of 10+ years experience in intellectual property law as a practitioner at a law firm and/or in-house legal department experience, with a substantial focus on patent prosecution.
At least 2+ years of in-house counsel experience strongly preferred, where responsibilities included patent portfolio management as well as IP-related transactions (with support of litigation and due diligence a plus).
Technical degree, professional background, and/or significant experience related to medical devices, robotics, mechanical engineering, or a related field (electrical engineering or other engineering specialties considered).
J.D. degree and membership in good standing with the California bar or eligible for immediate registration as a Registered In House Counsel “RHIC”.
Admitted to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
Ability to assess legal and business opportunities and risks related to IP assets in support of M&A, investment opportunities, licensing, and purchasing or selling of patent portfolios.
Exceptional communication and writing skills, able to distill complex technical and legal concepts for varied audiences.
Ability to closely manage outside counsel and control matter costs.
Willingness to travel on occasion as required.
Other Personal Characteristics:
Engaging, courageous, and self-directed, accustomed to managing with a collaborative, fact-based approach.
Collaborative, resourceful and adaptable—able to anticipate needs and navigate a rapidly changing environment.
Intellectually curious and eager to learn new areas of law and technology and apply knowledge effectively.
If you are ready to make an impact at the forefront of surgical technology innovation—and you have the drive to expand your expertise with a world-class team—we encourage you to apply.

Primary Function of Position
The Clinical Applications Engineer (CAE) reports to the Manager of Clinical Applications Engineering. The CAE plays a critical role in the early adoption of new technology, expanding access to robotic minimally invasive care. This individual will be primarily focused on building and supporting early users through their system learning curve and provide technical expertise on the system as applicable during clinical procedures. They will play a crucial role in transitioning users from their initial training to proficiency with the system and its use. They will also be responsible for providing guidance and perspective to design engineering about system usage nuances within the market they serve.
Essential Job Duties
• Provide procedural support to new robotic system sites to promote safety and effective progression
• Collaborate with global Clinical Applications Engineering and Endoluminal Sales to support new users through their early learning curve
• Provide expert clinical product and technical assistance and training to physicians and clinical staff on the effective use of Intuitive’s equipment during clinical procedures
• Identify key areas of concern for clinical users for procedure adoption and collaborate with training and development partners to evaluate and address them
• Drive collaboration and maintain consistent, open lines of communication across the assigned responsibilities with the global Clinical Applications Engineering team as well as the development teams.
• Collaborate with peers and development engineering partners to develop and share best practices and product feedback
• Stay current on company products instructions for use (IFU), best practices and technical troubleshooting, as well as relevant scientific clinical literature and new product information
• Prioritize and appropriately respond to requests in a high-stress environment.
Required Skills and Experience
• A minimum of 2 years of technical or clinical experience in healthcare
• Experience navigating hospitals and supporting procedures required
• Self-starter who performs well with autonomy and can be flexible in a dynamic work environment
• Problem solver who can maintain composure and think critically in high pressure environments
• Highly collaborative and works well in a remote team environment
• Effective communication skills including oral, written and interpersonal. Strong situational awareness

*In order to be considered for the role, candidates must reside in New York, NY, Boston, MA or Philadelphia, PA.*
Primary Function of Position
The Clinical Applications Engineer (CAE) reports to the Manager of Clinical Applications Engineering. The CAE plays a critical role in the early adoption of new technology, expanding access to robotic minimally invasive care. This individual will be primarily focused on building and supporting early users through their system learning curve and provide technical expertise on the system as applicable during clinical procedures. They will play a crucial role in transitioning users from their initial training to proficiency with the system and its use. They will also be responsible for providing guidance and perspective to design engineering about system usage nuances within the market they serve.
Essential Job Duties
• Provide procedural support to new robotic system sites to promote safety and effective progression
• Collaborate with global Clinical Applications Engineering and Endoluminal Sales to support new users through their early learning curve
• Provide expert clinical product and technical assistance and training to physicians and clinical staff on the effective use of Intuitive’s equipment during clinical procedures
• Identify key areas of concern for clinical users for procedure adoption and collaborate with training and development partners to evaluate and address them
• Drive collaboration and maintain consistent, open lines of communication across the assigned responsibilities with the global Clinical Applications Engineering team as well as the development teams.
• Collaborate with peers and development engineering partners to develop and share best practices and product feedback
• Stay current on company products instructions for use (IFU), best practices and technical troubleshooting, as well as relevant scientific clinical literature and new product information
• Prioritize and appropriately respond to requests in a high-stress environment.
Required Skills and Experience
• A minimum of 2 years of technical or clinical experience in healthcare
• Experience navigating hospitals and supporting procedures required
• Self-starter who performs well with autonomy and can be flexible in a dynamic work environment
• Problem solver who can maintain composure and think critically in high pressure environments
• Highly collaborative and works well in a remote team environment
• Effective communication skills including oral, written and interpersonal. Strong situational awareness
• Experience working with highly complex technical systems and/or working in a critical patient care setting with physicians and support staff
• Ability to seek out and process large amounts of data to translate information into actionable insights
• Desire to learn and build new skills
• Ability to travel up to 70%, located near a major airline/rail hub, and ability to work nights and weekends as needed
• Ability to independently prioritize and manage travel logistics, and complete associated administrative tasks in a timely manner
• Ability to travel on a moment’s notice and support cases across varying geographies; comfortable booking and utilizing all forms of travel
Required Education and Training
• Bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering or in healthcare-based field

Some experience in an academic environment conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of scientific data.

Excellent critical and analytical thinking skills.
Must have a high level of attention to detail and accuracy.

Strong presentation and interpersonal skills.
Ability to learn quickly and self-educate on different surgical specialties as applicable to medical products and procedures (Self-starter attitude)

Primary Function of Position
The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is searching for a Mechanical Engineer to help design the endoscope system for a novel robotic surgical platform. As an early member of the team, this role is an exciting opportunity to help define the eventual product from early prototypes through clinical trials and into product launch.
Essential Job Duties
As part of the New Product Development team, the engineer will work with team members to:
Distal Tip and Vision Mechanical Design
Own the mechanical design of the endoscope distal tip and camera module, including housings, optical windows, lens and image-sensor mounts, illumination (LED and/or fiber-optic) integration, and sealing features
Design miniature, high-precision machined, injection-molded / micro-molded, and MIM components; perform tolerance stack-up analysis to achieve tight optical alignment and high assembly yield
Select materials, adhesives, and joining processes (e.g., precision bonding, laser welding, soldering) compatible with biocompatibility, sterilization, and reliability requirements
Prototyping, Test, and Supplier Development
Rapidly build, assemble, and test prototypes; analyze results and drive fast design iterations
Apply FEA and other modeling and simulation methods (structural, thermal, sealing) to key design elements and use results to inform design decisions
Design tooling and fixtures for assembly, optical alignment, and test
Work with suppliers to take parts from quick-turn prototypes to production-intent components, driving DFM/DFA, quality, and cost
Requirements, Documentation, and Design Controls
Translate system and user needs into mechanical requirements and specifications; contribute to risk management activities (e.g., dFMEA)
Create detailed drawings with GD&T and document designs, test protocols, and reports under design controls (ISO 13485, FDA QMSR / 21 CFR 820)
Support design verification, clinical builds, and design transfer to manufacturing
Generate and evaluate concepts for next-generation endoscopic and vision devices
Electro-Mechanical and Thermal Integration
Partner with electrical engineers to package flex / rigid-flex circuits, micro-coax cables, and connectors through the tip and shaft, managing bend radius, strain relief, and EMI shielding
Perform thermal analysis (first-principles calculations and simulation) of the tip and camera module; design heat-spreading paths and heat sinks so that image sensors, patient-contacting surfaces remain within component and IEC 60601 temperature limits
Plan and execute thermal characterization tests (e.g., thermocouples, IR thermography) and correlate results with models
Required Skills and Experience
4+ years of industry experience designing and delivering complex, precision mechanical assemblies (or 1+ years with an PhD)
Hands-on experience building, assembling, and testing prototypes and complex mechanical assemblies
Proficiency in 3D CAD (SolidWorks strongly preferred) and detailed drawing creation
Working knowledge of GD&T (ASME Y14.5) / ISO drafting standards and tolerance stack-up analysis
Experience applying FEA and first-principles engineering analysis to the design of mechanical parts
Experience designing for machining and injection molding, and working directly with suppliers
Strong communication and documentation skills; proven ability to collaborate in a fast-paced, cross-functional team
Preferred Skills and Experience (Strong Plus)
Electro-mechanical system design: integrating PCBAs, flex / rigid-flex circuits, cabling, connectors, sensors, or actuators into compact mechanical packages
Thermal analysis and thermal management: heat-transfer calculations, heat sink / heat spreader sizing, and thermal simulation (e.g., ANSYS Icepak / Fluent, Simcenter FloTHERM, COMSOL, or SolidWorks Flow Simulation), with correlation to test data
Medical device development experience, particularly endoscopes, catheters, or other minimally invasive instruments, under ISO 13485 design controls
Knowledge of biocompatible materials (ISO 10993), sterilization / reprocessing methods, and sealing / ingress protection
Experience with micro-manufacturing processes such as Swiss-type machining, micro-molding, MIM, laser welding, and precision adhesive bonding
Familiarity with IEC 60601-1 and IEC 60601-2-18 (endoscopic equipment)
Scripting for data analysis or test automation (e.g., Python, MATLAB)

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
Intuitive Surgical designs and manufactures pioneering medical devices for use in surgery. These devices consist of surgical instruments, endoscopes, diagnostic tools, and accessories used on a robotic surgical platform. Each patient-contact device is evaluated for biological safety according to relevant international standards.  The Biological Safety Group at Intuitive are responsible for the definition, implementation, and communication of our biological safety program under the guidance of board-certified toxicologists.
The Biosafety Development Engineer is responsible for managing and collaborating with teams in support of the biological safety evaluation process for new products and changes to existing products. The successful candidate must excel in a high-energy, small-focused team environment, be a quick learner, and have a commitment to high product quality. The candidate must have a strong understanding of toxicology and analytical chemistry requirements for evaluating the biological safety of medical devices. The candidate should possess experience in designing and implementing biocompatibility safety evaluations, risk assessments, root-cause analysis, laboratory techniques, in vitro and in vivo test methods, and chemical analyses. The candidate should have experience in planning, tracking, creating process and procedure and implementing activities for the biological safety evaluation of medical devices, adhering to ISO 10993 guidelines. The candidate should have understating and knowledge of global regulatory requirements, compliance, quality management systems, audits, standards, and test methods for the biological safety evaluation and risk assessment of medical devices.
A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required and the ability to make work fun and interesting.  Supporting you will be a technical services management team that knows and cares about what you are doing and wants you to succeed.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Work closely with toxicologists and other specialists to support and implement the biological safety program at Intuitive; collaborate with biosafety group members to develop safety assessment plans.
Serve as the biological safety representative for new product development teams; attend meetings; communicate schedules; present at design reviews; and be responsible for peer interactions with engineering. With excellent organizational skills, prioritization abilities, and effective communication with project stakeholders, play a crucial role in managing multiple projects concurrently, ensuring the fulfillment of all compliance requirements.
Responsible for closely monitoring and ensuring that all processes and procedures are in line with the biocompatibility requirements set by relevant regulatory bodies. This includes conducting assessments, reviewing documentation, and implementing necessary changes to achieve compliance.
Support sustaining and supplier engineering programs by collecting information on design changes for patient-contact materials and coordinating the execution of biological safety assessment plans.
Responsible for continuously reviewing and updating biological safety processes and procedures based on current standards. This includes staying informed about the latest regulatory requirements and industry best practices to ensure our standards remain accurate and up to date.
Create and maintain project management tools to track biological safety activities and communicate progress on commitments to project leaders and business unit executives.
Responsible for establishing and maintaining a comprehensive tracking system for all compliance-related projects. This includes documenting project progress, milestones, and any necessary updates or changes. Ensure that all project documentation is easily accessible to the relevant stakeholders.
Engage directly with project stakeholders to address any requirements, processes, or compliance-related inquiries. able to effectively communicate complex information in a clear and concise manner will be crucial to ensuring a smooth compliance process.
Support biosafety plans, coordinate chemical characterization and biocompatibility testing activities at CRO laboratories; understand testing needs; request quotes; coordinate test articles; and track schedules.
Support the creation and archiving of documentation that supports the biological safety of intuitive products; write reports and release them in the document management system (Agile)
Maintain an ISI biological safety material database and provide computer-generated reports as needed.
Assist engineering teams in choosing patient-contact materials based on prior usage, and assist in describing design, material, process, and supplier modifications for biosafety evaluation.
The role involves supporting regulatory filing activities, including FDA 510(k) submissions (and other filing strategies), OUS country registration activities, MDR compliance certification, and other regulatory support needs.
Develop a working understanding of medical device biocompatibility, including relevant national and international standards, methods for biosafety end-point testing, and other regulatory requirements.
Skill/Job Requirements:
A minimum bachelor's degree in medical life science or engineering, or a master's degree, is preferred.
8+ years of experience in medical device product safety, product development, or related areas
Nice to Have:
Training in medical device biocompatibility testing and management, or an equivalent program, is preferred.
Proven project management skills: PMP certification is a plus.
Strong organizational and interpersonal skills are essential for working effectively in a team environment.
In vitro and in vivo laboratory testing experience is preferred but can be acquired through training.
Knowledge of MS Office applications

Primary Function of Position
The Senior Clinical Data Scientist will be part of the Ion business unit.  The Ion endoluminal system is Intuitive's robotic platform for minimally invasive biopsy in the peripheral lung, with an initial goal of improving the early diagnosis of lung cancer. The Senior Clinical Data Scientist sits at the intersection of clinical science and data science within the Ion business unit, translating clinical questions into rigorous, data-driven analyses that inform product strategy, evidence generation, and business decisions. This role reports to the Managing Staff, Clinical Data Science.
The individual in this role will partner with clinicians, cross-functional teams, and data engineering to design and execute a clinical data science strategy — defining hypotheses grounded in customer needs, identifying appropriate data sources, conducting quantitative analyses, and communicating results that demonstrably impact patient outcomes and business objectives. Unlike a purely clinical or purely technical role, this position demands both deep clinical understanding of the Ion platform and hands-on proficiency in modern data science methods and tools.
Success requires a strong technical foundation in Python or R, statistics, and causal reasoning; the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-evolving clinical and commercial landscape; and exceptional skill in communicating complex findings clearly — especially through polished visual presentations and well-organized documentation.
Essential Job Duties
Work with internal and external stakeholders (including clinicians, administrators, and policymakers) to identify data-centric needs in the clinical space and translate them into prioritized research questions with testable hypotheses.
Design, implement, and validate quantitative analyses in Python or R — applying appropriate statistical, machine learning, and causal inference methods to Ion device logs, clinical studies/registries, insurance claims databases, and EHR/EMR data — to test hypotheses.
Translate analyses into decision-useful stories, tailoring them to diverse groups of stakeholders — from technical peers building product, to senior leadership defining strategy, to external physicians looking to improve efficiency.
Demonstrate impact through internal/external reports, presentations, dashboards, peer-reviewed publications, and customer-facing deliverables.
Partner with cross-functional teams to assist with the design and execution of global clinical and economic evidence strategies, including designing and supporting clinical trials.
Support regulatory submissions by structuring and validating clinical datasets to meet FDA and EU MDR compliance standards.
Create and maintain well-organized, reproducible codebases with clear documentation, version control, and consistent coding standards.
Catalyze a data-driven culture internally — champion the use of data to generate compelling evidence and ultimately build a better product.
Required Skills and Experience
6+ years of experience with Master's degree or 4+ years with PhD in a quantitative, scientific, or engineering field (e.g., biostatistics, epidemiology, data science, computer science, biomedical engineering, public health, or a related discipline). MD with quantitative research experience also accepted.
Experience with Python or R for data analysis, statistical modeling, and visualization.
Working knowledge of SQL for querying and managing structured datasets.
Demonstrated experience with causal inference methods and study design.
Experience working with device-generated log data, clinical study/registry data, and claims/EHR-style databases.
Experience with causal inference in a healthcare or medical device context.
Experience using platforms such as Snowflake or Databricks for production-level data pipelines and analytics.
Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) for the presentation of complex data to non-technical stakeholders or regulatory bodies.
Experience with Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems (e.g., Medrio) for managing clinical study/registry data.
Experience using AI/ML tools to accelerate software development and data analysis workflows.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to frame ambiguous clinical questions as testable hypotheses and select fit-for-purpose methods.
Stellar organizational skills, particularly with respect to code management and documentation.
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, including clinicians, engineers, regulatory, commercial, and data science partners.
Self-starter attitude with the ability to manage multiple priorities, operate independently, and deliver under ambiguity.
Track record of peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations in clinical research or data science.
Experience in medical devices or other regulated industries.
Familiarity with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ISO 14155 (clinical investigation of medical devices), and data privacy regulations (HIPAA/GDPR).
Familiarity with the lung cancer landscape (screening, diagnosis, treatment).

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About the Team
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive's advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery. Our research team is building advanced augmented dexterity capabilities for next-generation robotic platforms.
The Role
Our researchers should spend their time on ideas, not on the manual work required to turn those ideas into results on real robots.
As a Senior AI & Automation Engineer, you will build the AI tools, automation systems, integrations, and evaluation capabilities that help researchers and engineers train, test, and evaluate models faster and make better decisions. You'll leverage existing AI technologies while developing new solutions, from agent-driven workflows and AI tooling to the APIs, services, and automation frameworks that support engineering and research activities.
That could mean agents that set up and run experiments, automation workflows that accelerate testing and evaluation, or tools that sort through logs and video to help teams understand failures and improve outcomes. It's a hands-on engineering role that uses AI to improve how physical AI systems are trained and tested. You'll automate that work; you won't design the models themselves. You'll work closely with ML researchers, simulation engineers, and robotics engineers.
What You'll Do
• Build and integrate AI tools, APIs, and agent workflows that automate engineering and research work across the team.
• Automate the training and fine-tuning workflow, from setting up experiments to launching, tracking, and comparing runs, so researchers can reproduce results without hand-built scripts.
• Build automation and integration workflows that help researchers and engineers evaluate new ideas in simulation and on real robots, quickly, reliably, and at scale.
• Design evaluations and experiments that show, with statistical confidence, whether a change is a real improvement.
• Build logging, analysis, and debugging tools that help the team understand results and failures, and that turn robot sessions into data the team can train on.
• Make what you build reliable, secure, and safe to run, with human approval where it matters and responsible use of AI throughout.
• Evaluate emerging AI tools, models, and technologies, and bring in the ones that deliver measurable impact.
• Measure the impact of what you build, document it clearly, and make successful tools part of how the team operates.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these areas than shallow coverage of all of them.
• Hands-on work with real robots. You've built testing, automation, or evaluation systems that ran on real robot hardware or other physical systems via software interfaces, not only in the cloud or in simulation.
• AI and automation you've built and put into daily use. You've built LLM-agent workflows, AI tool integrations, copilots, or automation pipelines for real engineering work and measured whether they helped. Be ready to walk us through one: what it did, where it failed, and what you changed.
• Evaluation and experimental rigor. You know how to design experiments and understand the statistics needed to determine whether an improvement is real.
• Strong software engineering. You have 5+ years of software engineering experience.
You write production-quality Python, can read C++, and are comfortable with Linux, CI/CD, Docker, containerized services, APIs, and distributed systems.
Strong candidates often come from robotics, autonomous systems, physical AI, or robot- learning research, and have applied AI tooling to real hardware. You're comfortable working across disciplines in a fast-moving research environment and can explain trade-offs clearly to researchers and engineers alike.
If you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you.
Education
• BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical
Engineering, or a related technical field.
• Advanced degree (MS or PhD) preferred.
Bonus Points
None of these are required. They're signals, not gates, and any one of them is a nice plus.
• Robotics simulation, such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab or MuJoCo
• Evaluating AI/ML, robotics, or robot-learning systems
• Surgical or medical robotics, including da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) systems
• ROS 2 or other robot middleware
• Agent frameworks, tool integrations, or MCP servers adopted by engineering teams
• AI assistants, copilots, or productivity tools built for engineers or researchers
• AI applied to scientific, engineering, or research workflows

description:

Primary Function of Position
The Ion™ endoluminal system is Intuitive's new robotic platform for minimally invasive biopsy in the peripheral lung, with an initial goal of improving the early diagnosis of lung cancer. We are seeking a senior algorithm engineer to play a lead technical role in conceptualizing, designing, and evaluating our next-generation planning and guidance software. This role is dedicated to developing advanced algorithms to analyze chest medical images for complex lung diseases. This role focuses heavily on the processing and fusion of diverse imaging modalities—including CT, CBCT, and X-ray images—to perform robust lung structure segmentation, system navigation, target localization, ultimately improving clinical outcomes.
Essential Job Duties:
Drive the full cycle of medical imaging analysis software development, developing algorithms from R&D concepts into robust, commercial medical device products.
Design, prototype, and implement advanced medical imaging and machine learning algorithms tailored for advanced lung structure segmentation, registration, target localization, respiratory anomaly detection, and bronchial analysis.
Apply and fine-tune state-of-the-art architectures, including nnU-Net, Vision Transformers (ViTs), DINO, Diffusion models, and Vision Language Models (VLMs), for clinical datasets.
Architect and execute model deployment pipelines, seamlessly integrating trained models into high-performance C++ production environments, utilizing techniques like quantization, pruning, and hardware acceleration to ensure real-time performance on constrained medical systems.
Support system integration and testing while generating formal design documentation and patent applications.

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field.
5+ years of hands-on industrial experience in algorithm development, with a deep specialization in medical imaging and computer vision. A proven track record of shipping commercial AI/ML software products is bonus.
Exceptional proficiency in Python and C++, with a deep understanding of modern software component design for production environments.
Proven hands-on experience with ML frameworks and software toolkits, including PyTorch, OpenCV, MONAI, ITK, VTK, and model optimization tools such as TensorRT or ONNX.
Experience or knowledge of the development of AI/ML features in strict alignment with Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP) principles, ensuring data representativeness and model transparency.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective cross-functional collaboration with clinical and engineering teams.

The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.
Lead subsystem architecture decisions. Compare alternatives and justify tradeoffs.
Design precision mechanisms, joints and actuation assemblies. Select and size components such as motors, bearings, transmissions, brakes and sensors based on operating loads, motion requirements and expected life.
Use first-principles calculations and simulation to establish load paths, component margins, structural stiffness, dynamic behavior and fatigue life. Check assumptions and correlate models with test results.
Create and release CAD models, manufacturing drawings and design documentation. Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis to functional interfaces, assembly requirements and inspection.
Build, test, debug and iterate prototypes. Develop test methods and fixtures, investigate failures, and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers, supplier engineering, sourcing and manufacturing to resolve technical issues, improve DFM/DFA and cost, and prepare designs for transfer.
Collaborate with systems, electrical, controls, clinical, human factors, manufacturing, supplier engineering/sourcing, quality and regulatory partners to resolve requirements and subsystem interfaces.
Lead technical reviews and guide other engineers’ design and analysis approaches. Plan technical work across functions, set priorities, resolve risks and mentor engineers through problem-solving.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 14 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 10 years, or a PhD plus 6 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
Working Conditions
On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.
Travel: 10%, including occasional visits to supplier and manufacturing sites.
Preferred Skills and Experience
The following skills and experience are not required but represent attributes of an ideal candidate.
Experience developing Class II or Class III medical devices, particularly surgical robotics or medical device capital equipment.
Direct application of standards and documentation frameworks such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), IEC 60601, ISO 14971, and DHF.
Experience supporting production launch, manufacturing scale-up or post-launch reliability investigations, and applying those lessons to new product designs.

title: Systems Analyst (Robotic Algorithms and Control)
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Join Multi-Port System Design Engineering, the team that brought the da Vinci 5 system to life and is building what comes next. Learn more at https://careers.intuitive.com/en/career-opportunities/engineering/multiport-engineering/
Primary Function of Position
Systems Analysts (Robotic Algorithms and Control) at Intuitive Surgical perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the daVinci Surgery product line. Systems Analysts are primarily responsible for the tele-robotic motion control algorithms, robotic manipulator control, interaction behaviors, and safety algorithms for new surgical robots and surgical instruments. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering where all the subsystems are integrated together. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, quickly prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to subtle and challenging problems in system integration and motion control. Responsibilities continue until the products are shipping to customers with the highest quality and reliability.
Essential Job Duties
Contribute to design of new surgical platforms and instruments through control system analysis and characterization of prototypes.
Design and implement motion algorithms and behaviors.
Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.
Create safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Document and pursue intellectual property.
Communicate system performance to the organization as a whole.
Improve group work-flow through tool building and teaching others.
Support and track system performance as it moves from design through manufacturing.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure performance requirements are relevant, measurable, and realistic.
Required Skills and Experience
Advanced knowledge of classical and modern control theory, with hands-on experience implementing control systems in safety critical products.
Demonstrated experience with robotic manipulation algorithms, including learning-based/ML approaches.
Strong embedded C/C++ and system integration experience (hardware + firmware/software + mechanisms).
Strong engineering intuition for mechatronic systems, paired with attention to detail and the ability to drive solutions to completion.
Ability to excel in a high-energy team environment, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while balancing collaboration on project planning, execution, and communication.
Passion for product quality and continuous improvements.
Required Education and Training
3 years experience and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 1 years experience; or equivalent experience.
