OR equivalent experience.
8+ years of experience in Data Science, Applied Statistics, Quantitative Analytics, Machine Learning, Operations Research, Sales Analytics, or a related quantitative field.
Experience developing complex statistical, forecasting, optimization, or machine-learning models.
Proficient programming and analytical skills using Python, R, SQL, KQL, or comparable languages.
Experience analyzing large datasets and translating quantitative findings into actionable business recommendations.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Overview
The Agent 365 Foundation team builds and operates the platform layer that keeps agent workloads reliable, secure, and fast at Microsoft scale. Our charter within this group is traffic ingress: every request that reaches our clusters passes through the gateway and edge systems we own. We are the front door, which means we are also the first line of defense and the first place a problem shows up.
A significant part of our current focus is ingress for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic. That work spans routing and gateway policy, connection and protocol handling, tenant isolation, throttling and abuse mitigation, failover behavior across regions, and the observability needed to reason about all of it while it is happening. The scale is large, the traffic patterns are diverse, and the correctness bar is high.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and operate the gateway and ingress path end to end. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will spend your time in code, in design reviews, and in production — writing services in C# and Go, tuning TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, shaping how gRPC traffic flows through the stack, working with Azure Front Door and our own edge components, and hardening the system against volumetric and application-layer attacks.
You will own outcomes rather than tickets. That means choosing where resiliency belongs in the request path, deciding what a safe failure mode looks like for a given class of traffic, and defending those decisions with data. You will also be part of the on-call rotation for the systems you build, because the fastest way to build a resilient front door is to feel it when it bends.
Who Thrives in This Role
The engineer who does well here is genuinely hands-on. You are comfortable being the person who reads the proxy source, reproduces the failure locally, and lands the fix — seniority here means more time close to the system, not less. You think critically about problems before reaching for a solution, ask what the data actually shows, and are willing to challenge a design, including your own, when the evidence points elsewhere.
You also do not shy away from hard problems. Ambiguous incidents, legacy traffic paths, unfamiliar protocol behavior, and difficult cross-team conversations are part of the work, and you move toward them rather than around them. You are direct, collaborative, and comfortable operating with a high degree of ownership.
Why This Role Matters
Ingress is where reliability and security are decided for everything behind it. The work you do here is visible in the availability numbers of some of Microsoft's largest business platforms, and it is felt immediately by the customers who depend on them. If you want a role where deep networking expertise, sound judgment, and engineering craft compound into real impact, this is it.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Design, implement, and operate L4 and L7 ingress components — gateways, proxies, load balancing and routing policy — that carry Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic into our clusters.
Own the protocol layer: TLS termination and certificate lifecycle, HTTP/2 connection management, gRPC routing and streaming behavior, and the performance characteristics of each.
Build resiliency into the request path through health-based routing, retries and hedging, circuit breaking, load shedding, rate limiting, and regional failover, and prove the behavior through fault injection and load testing.
Strengthen the security posture of the edge, including DDoS detection and mitigation, WAF and abuse-mitigation policy, tenant isolation, and defense against application-layer attack patterns.
Integrate and tune Azure Front Door and related edge services alongside our first-party gateway components, and make deliberate decisions about which layer solves which problem.
Instrument the ingress path so that latency, error, and saturation questions can be answered in minutes, and drive incident response, root-cause analysis, and the follow-through that keeps the same failure from repeating.
Partner with service teams across Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Agent 365 on onboarding, capacity, and traffic-shaping decisions, and raise the engineering bar through design and code review.

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.

As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications. Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Asks questions when they do not have required information, resolves others' questions in a timely manner, and may provide feedback on changes to processes to direct-line management.

Participates in the regular cadence of proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Mentors other Support Escalation team members on how to handle moderate to highly complex cases. Owns incident communications, customer, governance, and post?incident insights. Customer Resolution
Identifies trends across internal postmortems and suggests resources to drive opportunities within the team and across stakeholder groups in post-incident review discussions to remediate future issues. Identifies risks surfaced during escalations and ensures they are routed to proper governance channels within or outside of their Strategic Business Unit (SBU). Ensures remediation includes thorough root cause analysis and any corrective follow-ups required. Acts on or plays a key role in strategic projects designed to improve resolution times, customer satisfaction, and support experience. Implements AI tools to monitor, evaluate, and automate routine tasks, proposing enhancements to boost efficiency and satisfaction. Identifies systemic breakdowns across escalation workflows, handoffs, and decision points, and drives cross?team improvements to increase speed, accountability, and consistency. Champions automation and standardization of escalation workflows to improve scale and consistency. Creates home-grown solutions for intake, tracking and reporting for customer businesses. Provides status updates to customers and internal stakeholders through various channels of communication regarding issues, following the documented process. Utilizes AI-driven communication tools streamline interactions with stakeholders. Coordinates and communicates the escalation narrative, ensuring stakeholder alignment and driving Confidence Calls to either retain customers, solidify renewals, or take direct feedback on the product or support. Drives consistent, executive-ready escalation narrative, aligning all stakeholders on problem statement, impact, risks, and next actions. Acts as a primary contact to understand issues and improve the experiences of customers independently. Maintains and develops relationships with various internal and external teams to resolve customer issues. Mentors others on the Support Escalation Management team. Acts as a key member of projects to drive key strategic initiatives. Manages incidents, which are customer-impacting issues that require coordination, communication, and stakeholder/resource management to drive timely resolution. Owns the end-to-end escalation lifecycle, where escalations are incidents that require elevated visibility or intervention that involve direct engagement with customers or senior stakeholders, including intake, triage, prioritization, resolution, and follow-up. Supports the lifecycle of incidents, which is the coordination, communication, and stakeholder/resource management. Represents Microsoft, Leadership or Strategic Business Unit (SBU) Leaders on internal/external calls. Leverage AI-driven sentiment analysis tools to gather real-time feedback, identify common customer pain points, and suggest proactive measures for enhancing customer service. OpenAI's Global Affairs team works to ensure that artificial intelligence benefits people, communities, and countries around the world. We engage with policymakers, institutions, and stakeholders to help shape the policies and partnerships that enable AI to expand economic opportunity, accelerate innovation, and deliver broad public benefits.

About the Role

We are seeking an Analytics Manager to help Global Affairs develop and communicate data-driven insights into how people and businesses are using ChatGPT, with a particular focus on local and regional trends across the United States and other priority markets.

In this role, you will analyze privacy-protective, aggregated usage data to identify meaningful patterns in AI adoption and use. You'll explore how people are using AI to work, learn, create, build businesses, and solve everyday problems, translating complex datasets into accessible insights that support policy development, strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, and public education.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical skills with an instinct for what makes data meaningful to policymakers, journalists, business leaders, and the public. You should be comfortable working with large datasets, identifying compelling patterns, evaluating the limitations of available evidence, and collaborating with policy and communications colleagues to turn findings into clear, credible narratives.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys moving between quantitative analysis, strategic problem-solving, and storytelling. You'll have the opportunity to help build a new analytical capability within Global Affairs and shape how OpenAI understands and communicates the adoption and use of AI across different communities.

This role is based in San Francisco, Washington, DC, or an approved remote location. Work arrangements and relocation eligibility will depend on the approved location.

Develop Local and Regional Insights

 - Analyze approved, aggregated ChatGPT usage data to identify geographic patterns in AI adoption and use, including trends across states, metropolitan areas, and other markets where the data supports reliable analysis.

 - Develop insights into how people are using AI for education, workforce development, entrepreneurship, small business activities, professional productivity, and other areas of economic and social opportunity.

title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy
description:
About the Team

The Product Policy research team studies how people use and experience AI, generating evidence to inform product, policy, and safety decisions. We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

 - Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

 - Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

 - Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

 - Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

 - Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

 - Support human-subjects research review, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) documentation, protocol amendments, and consent and assent processes.

 - Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

 - Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience conducting applied quantitative research in social science, behavioral science, human-computer interaction, statistics, or a related field.

 - Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

 - Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

 - Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

 - Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

 - Communicate clearly, lead with the key takeaway, and connect methodological choices and findings to the decisions they inform.

 - Exercise sound judgment when working with sensitive data and research involving minors.

 - Enjoy building structure in ambiguous environments and collaborating across disciplines.

 - Experience combining survey responses with behavioral or product data.

 - Familiarity with preregistration, measure validation, reproducible research, and academic publication or peer-review processes.

 - Experience working with research vendors, survey platforms, or IRB and ethics-review partners.

 - Research experience related to AI-human interaction, digital well-being, youth development, or social and emotional uses of technology.

We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work.

About the role

As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny.

Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio.

You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements.

 - Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths.

 - Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments.

 - Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision.

 - Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why.

 - Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance.

 - Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners.

 - Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs.

 - Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority.

 - Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal.

The Compute & Infrastructure team shares financial insights and partners with internal and external business stakeholders to manage the accounting and financial reporting for OpenAI’s rapidly evolving infrastructure investments.

The team supports a broad and increasingly complex portfolio of compute and infrastructure arrangements, including cloud computing, data centers, servers, equipment, rack financing, colocation arrangements, and other AI infrastructure deployments. We are responsible for ensuring financial accuracy, operational scalability, and informed decision-making as OpenAI continues to invest in advanced technologies and expand its infrastructure footprint.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and technically skilled accounting professional to manage the accounting and financial reporting for OpenAI’s compute and infrastructure lease-related activities. In this role, you will own complex lease accounting matters across data centers, servers, equipment, and other infrastructure arrangements, while helping operationalize new programs as the organization continues to scale.

You will evaluate unique and highly structured transactions, assess their accounting implications, and translate technical conclusions into clear recommendations for leadership. You will also work cross-functionally to design the processes, systems, controls, and data solutions required to support accurate and scalable accounting operations.

This role requires a strong command of US GAAP, particularly lease accounting and consolidation, as well as the ability to operate effectively and fluidly in an evolving environment where new infrastructure programs may not yet have established processes or system solutions. The ideal candidate is both a technical accounting expert and a hands-on builder who can turn complex arrangements into sustainable operating models.

You will partner closely with Finance, Technical Accounting, Legal, Tax, Procurement, Engineering, Infrastructure, and other key stakeholders. You will also work with external counterparties and service providers to ensure the accounting treatment, operational processes, and reporting outputs are accurate, well-documented, and scalable.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Own the end-to-end accounting for compute and infrastructure lease-related activities, including data centers, servers, equipment, colocation arrangements, and other infrastructure deployments.

 - Evaluate new and evolving infrastructure arrangements to determine the appropriate accounting treatment under US GAAP, including lease identification, classification, measurement, commencement, modification, impairment, and presentation considerations.

 - Partner with Technical Accounting and other cross-functional stakeholders to assess complex or non-standard transactions, document accounting conclusions, and present the financial reporting implications to senior leadership.

 - Lead the accounting operationalization of new compute and infrastructure programs by developing scalable processes, controls, systems, data requirements, and reporting solutions from the ground up.

 - Design and implement system solutions to support lease accounting, fixed asset tracking, subledger requirements, data integration, and management reporting.

 - Own month-end and quarter-end close activities for the lease portfolio, including journal entries, reconciliations, flux analysis, rollforwards, balance sheet substantiation, and reporting packages.

 - Ensure the completeness and accuracy of lease-related accounting records by developing robust contract intake, asset tracking, and reconciliation processes.

 - Manage the accounting and reporting requirements for unique legal entities and special-purpose structures associated with infrastructure investments, including consolidation assessments, intercompany activity, and entity-level reporting.

 - Monitor changes in contractual arrangements and operational facts to identify lease modifications, reassessments, impairments, consolidation changes, and other accounting impacts.

 - Build and maintain strong internal controls over lease accounting, infrastructure data, entity reporting, journal entries, reconciliations, and management review processes.

 - Support internal and external audit requests, including preparation of accounting documentation, control evidence, reconciliation support, and responses to technical questions.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 10+ years of progressive experience in accounting, audit, advisory, or a related finance function, with meaningful experience managing complex transactions from initial assessment through operational execution.

 - Strong technical knowledge of US GAAP, particularly ASC 842, ASC 810, ASC 360, fixed asset accounting, construction-in-progress accounting, and related financial reporting requirements.

 - Experience assessing complex lease arrangements, embedded leases, equipment financing, data center arrangements, build-to-suit structures, or other infrastructure-related transactions.

 - Experience with consolidation accounting, including variable interest entity assessments, special-purpose entities, intercompany accounting, and noncontrolling interests.

 - Demonstrated ability to translate complex contractual terms and accounting conclusions into scalable operational processes, system requirements, and control frameworks.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

 - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

 - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

 - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

 - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

 - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

 - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

 - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

 - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

 - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

 - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

 - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

 - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

 - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet.

 - Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer.

 - Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. Track false failures, cycle time, and uptime against agreed improvement targets.

 - Release hardware documentation, versioned test code, commissioning checks, and troubleshooting procedures that enable lab and contract-manufacturer teams to reproduce, operate, and maintain the station

description:
About the Team

The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company’s long-term trajectory. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-To-Market teams to inform high-stakes decisions through rigorous data science and economic modeling. As part of our expanding Data Science function, we’re building a best-in-class Forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.

 

We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives. You’ll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.

 

This is a highly cross-functional role, requiring technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Build statistical and machine learning models to solve forecasting needs across product, finance, infrastructure, and GTM domains.

 - Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.

 - Develop and productionize scalable, interpretable forecasts for user growth, monetization, compute load, customer lifetime value, and profitability.

 - Contribute to self-service forecasting tools and internal platforms, enabling teams across OpenAI to access and act on real-time predictions.

 - Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space, such as TimeGPT, large language model extensions, causal forecasting, and hybrid approaches.

 - Drive strategic insight generation by translating technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure forecasts are well-integrated into planning processes, experimentation workflows, and executive decision-making.





You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).

 - 7+ years of experience in applied data science, with deep hands-on exposure to forecasting, predictive modeling, or marketplace systems.

 - Expertise in time-series forecasting techniques and practical understanding of model trade-offs across performance, explainability, and scalability.

 - Proficiency in Python, SQL, and tools such as scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow, and forecasting libraries.

 - Demonstrated experience with model monitoring, debugging, and long-term maintenance in production environments.

 - Strong communication and storytelling skills - able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.

 - Self-directed, intellectually curious, and comfortable leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.

 

Bonus if you have:

 - Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

 - Familiarity with causal inference, Bayesian forecasting.

 - Experience building agentic decision support systems.

 - Passion for AI and a strong point of view on how machine learning should inform strategic decisions in fast-moving environments.

You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

 - Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

 - Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

 - Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

 - Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

 - Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

 - Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

 - Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

 - Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

 - Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

title: Staff AI Engineer
description:
Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
About the role
Oura is rebuilding how it builds software. Every engineer has agentic tooling, and our own pipeline already takes a well-formed ticket to a reviewed, tested commit stack. It runs interactively, headless, and on a cloud sandbox fleet, with its own evals and tracing. We are looking for engineers who use AI as a fundamental building block of both the products we ship and the way we build them.
That is a strong start on one stage of the lifecycle. The next step is the whole loop. As a Staff Engineer on the AI Transformation team, you will architect and own the system that turns agentic development from something power users do into the way hundreds of engineers across iOS, Android, backend and AI services ship every day. That means spec and intake, planning, implementation, review, testing, CI/CD, release, observability and incident follow-up, each with agents doing real work and humans keeping judgment where it matters.
This is a fast-moving, LLM-forward team. We prioritize rapid prototyping, iterative loops and AI-native development, with the speed of a startup and the reach of a product used by millions of members. You can work remotely from anywhere in Europe, or hybrid from our offices in Helsinki, Oulu or Tampere.
You will build the pipeline, measure it, and make it trustworthy enough that teams choose it. Success is measured in validated changes reaching members faster and safer: time to a trustworthy signal, escaped defects, cost per merged change, and how many squads run on the paved path because it is better, not because they were told to.
What you will do
You don't need to do all of these on day one, but these are the kinds of problems you'll own:
Set the technical direction for the agentic pipeline: Make our existing ticket-to-PR pipeline dependable infrastructure. Own its architecture, including agent orchestration, context management and tool calling, and improve its reliability, throughput, cost and developer experience across mobile, backend and web repositories. Run it unattended where the risk allows.
Close the loop across the SDLC: Extend agentic workflows beyond code generation into spec quality checks, test generation, automated review, CI failure triage and repair, release verification, and post-deploy signals, so the system improves from what happens after merge.
Prototype fast, then harden: Get a new workflow running in days, prove it on real tickets with real squads, and turn what holds up into production infrastructure.
Run AI in production properly: Agents in production take more than an API call. Own the eval sets, LLM-as-a-judge grading, versioning, tracing and dashboards that tell us whether a workflow change made things better, including the hardest case: a change that passes CI and is still wrong. Track the numbers that matter (merge rate, rework, time-to-signal, cost per change, escaped defects) and make them visible to engineers and leadership.
Make autonomy safe: Design sandboxing, permissions, human checkpoints and guardrails proportional to risk, with privacy by design as the default. Health data, security and infrastructure changes get stronger controls; low-risk, easily verified work runs hands-off.
Lead AI-native engineering by example: Set the bar for AI-augmented engineering across the organization. Show in your own work what a pipeline-first engineer ships, and raise the craft of the engineers around you.
Drive adoption with the teams: Embed with squads and their AI DRIs, find where the pipeline breaks on real work, fix the system rather than the single output, and turn what works into paved paths, skills, templates and docs other engineers can extend.
Partner cross-functionally: Work with platform, developer productivity, security and privacy, AI infrastructure, mobile and backend squads, product and design, and engineering leadership to make trade-offs explicit and keep everyone moving on one system instead of five parallel ones.
Requirements
We'd love to hear from you if you are:
An experienced builder: 6+ years building and operating production systems that other engineers depend on, including developer tooling, internal platforms, or AI infrastructure at scale. We weigh demonstrated outcomes over years.
Proven with agentic loops in production: You have built and operated agentic coding workflows or autonomous loops in a real engineering organization, beyond demos: background agents producing PRs, automated review, CI repair, test generation, or similar, with adoption and measured results.
A whole-lifecycle thinker: You reason about specification, review, testing, CI/CD, release and operations as one system, and you know where the bottleneck moves when code generation gets cheap.
A technical leader: You set direction across teams you don't manage, write the designs others build on, and are trusted with the hard calls on architecture and risk.
Strong on fundamentals: mobile domain or backend APIs, concurrency, distributed systems, testing, debugging and reliability. You treat AI output as a draft and can show how you verify it.
Technically versatile: Fluency in one domain of backend, iOS, or Android, with a stretch into others. You use the tools available to work across platforms and pick up new stacks quickly.
Security and privacy conscious: You understand the responsibility of handling sensitive personal data and of giving agents access to real systems, and you design for both from the start.
High agency: You thrive in ambiguity and shape the requirements yourself through experimentation.
Collaborative and resilient: You bring teams along, take feedback from engineers who are skeptical, share credit, and keep going when experiments fail or the tooling changes under you. You communicate clearly with engineers, managers and non-engineering partners.
Nice to Haves
You don't need all of these, but they're nice signals of fit:
Experience with coding agents at depth: skills, MCP servers, hooks, sub-agent orchestration, headless runs.
Built evaluation harnesses or benchmarks for coding agents, or LLM-as-judge grading tied to build and test outcomes.
Experience with sandboxed execution at scale: ephemeral dev environments, VM or container fleets, macOS build infrastructure.
Background in developer productivity measurement (DORA, SPACE, DX Core 4) and in turning metrics into decisions without turning them into targets.
Shipped to mobile apps or other environments with slow, expensive feedback loops.
Experience in digital health, wearables, MedTech, or other privacy-sensitive or regulated products.
Contributions to open-source AI projects, or a portfolio of projects built on the latest agent capabilities.
Mentored engineers or led an engineering community of practice.

title: Software Engineer II - Growth
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Software Engineer II, Growth
We are seeking a Software Engineer II for the Growth Marketing Engineering Team. You are the kind of engineer who gravitates toward the hardest problems at the intersection of technology and performance marketing: designing a low-latency bidding optimization engine, building a reliable creative generation pipeline, or defining the architectural patterns that will shape how Quince scales its growth stack. You operate with high autonomy, hold yourself to exceptional standards, and naturally raise the bar for the engineers around you through rigorous code reviews, sharp technical judgment, and a bias toward clean, durable solutions over quick fixes.
Responsibilities
Designing and implementing software features and components, following best practices and coding standards with minimal supervision.
Contributing to identifying the root cause of complex problems, scale, and stability challenges.
Proposing a solution to mitigate them in the short/medium/long term horizon.
Keeping up-to-date with new technologies, frameworks, and best practices in software development, and applying them to improve the performance and reliability of software systems.
Writing and maintaining technical documentation, API specifications, code documentation, and technical design documents.
Participating in code reviews and contributing to the development of coding standards and best practices.
Mentoring junior engineers and contributing to their professional growth and development.
Leading software development projects and working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality software products
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
At least 2 years of professional experience working in building user facing products.
Experience in advertisement performance tooling is a plus.
Proficient in using debugging tools and techniques.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
Understand the hustle of a startup and are good with handling ambiguity.
Effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Curious, quick learner, scrappy and someone who loves to experiment.

title: AI Data Operation Lead,  Autonomy
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary Rivian Autonomy is seeking an AI Data Operation Lead to lead the people and processes that turn vehicle data into reliable training and evaluation datasets. Within the AI Platform organization, you will bring together labeling delivery, data quality, curation, and human review to support the development of our autonomous driving models. You will lead internal teams and external partners, with accountability for delivery, quality, and cost. This includes making sure the data we send for annotation is usable, that accepted labels meet the model teams' requirements, and that reviewers can turn difficult driving events into actionable feedback for engineering. You will work closely with Perception, Planning, Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Product to translate model-development priorities into operational plans and provide evidence for release decisions. We are looking for a leader who can develop managers and specialists, make clear tradeoffs when demand exceeds capacity, and build an operation that improves as our models, tools, and vehicle fleet evolve. Responsibilities Lead the organization. Set the operating plan for AI data operations, develop team leaders, and define responsibilities across employees, contractors, and vendors. Build capacity plans that account for annotation, quality review, and rework across concurrent programs. Deliver data that model teams can use. Translate training and evaluation needs into labeling specifications, reviewer guidance, delivery milestones, and acceptance criteria. Work with model teams on taxonomy changes and keep delivery aligned with their development cycles. Improve data quality and yield. Own the operational checks that determine whether collected vehicle data is ready for curation and labeling. Partner with collection and engineering teams to resolve sensor, calibration, and data-quality issues before they consume downstream annotation capacity. Own vendor performance and spend. Set service levels and quality expectations, evaluate suppliers, and manage capacity, pricing, and budgets with Finance and Procurement. Reconcile accepted work with invoices and address delivery or quality shortfalls through clear corrective actions. Develop human evaluation and triage operations. Build review workflows with autonomy and systems engineers to investigate driving events, classify recurring failures, and assemble the evidence needed for root-cause analysis. Feed those findings into scenario selection, evaluation datasets, and targeted data requests. Run the operation with consistent metrics. Establish a shared view of accepted-data volume, quality, turnaround time, backlog, rework, collection yield, and cost. Use these measures to identify constraints, allocate review capacity, and make delivery commitments teams can plan around. Improve tools and automation. Partner with Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Applied General AI on labeling tools, prelabels, automated quality checks, and assisted triage. Define operational requirements and validate improvements against measured quality and reviewer effort before scaling them. Qualifications 10+ years leading operations, including at least 5 years supporting autonomous vehicles, robotics, or complex machine-learning programs, with responsibility for budgets or a P&L. description:
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively.

Overtime may be required based on business needs

Join Our Team as an Assembler!
Are you passionate about assembly? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Vista & Vista SD Assembly team. As an Assembler, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team.
In this job, you will assemble VISTA units and corresponding subassemblies. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity, and must meet requirements within time constraints. This is an assembly line operation involving as many as six stations. Initially you will be assigned to one station but will need to be flexible and open to working additional stations as business needs require. Tasks require a high degree of eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity, and the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion. You will frequently use hand and power tools; occasionally work while standing on ladders; and occasionally work inside tight compartments.
Key Responsibilities:
Assemble VISTA Switch, both on the assembly line and directly on the shop floor.
Identify, transport, install, mount and bolt all types of components (ranging from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs., with assistance), including bus assemblies, high-voltage switches, mounting and support plates, lock assemblies,
Perform mechanical inspection using torque wrenches, screwdrivers, and tape measures.
Have proficiency in the use of simple material handling equipment, hand tools, power tools, simple gauges, instruments and overhead cranes.
Operate simple machinery such as automatic Press machines.
Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, blueprints, and manufacturing drawings.
Measure, cut, route, bundle, and label wires according to engineering specifications.
Use hand tools and specialized equipment such as crimpers, wire strippers, cutters, heat guns, and torque tools.
Crimp terminals, lugs, connectors, and other electrical components in accordance with established standards.
Verify wire sizes, colors, routing, and terminations against drawings and work instructions.
Conduct continuity checks and basic electrical inspections to ensure proper assembly.
Identify and report material shortages, drawing discrepancies, quality concerns, or process issues.
Work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Production teams to meet customer and production requirements.
What you’ll Need to Succeed:
High School/GED diploma required.
Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.
Demonstrated ability to use basic shop math and measurement tools such as tape measures.
Ability to follow standard work instructions, assembly drawings, and specifications.
Knowledge and ability to use air impact tools and other hand-held tools.
2 years of mechanical assembly and/or electrical wiring experience. Candidates with electrical or mechanical trade school education may also be considered.
Preferred:
Previous experience in an assembly or manufacturing environment a plus.
Physical demands:
Standing: All tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional pushing of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Pulling: Occasional pulling of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching to safely lift parts of various sizes and shapes.
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Other: Respirator certification required.

About the role:
Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.
Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.
This is a remote  position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.
Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.
Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.
Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

title: Business Operations Generalist
description:
COMPANY BACKGROUND

Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.




THE ROLE

We are looking for a Business Operations Generalist to join Specter's lean BizOps team. This person will work across deal support, pricing, market strategy, planning, finance, and company systems. Today the work leans more commercial, including working with our GTM teams on sales materials, customer value cases, and proposals. In a given week, it can mean a customer business case one day and a CRM cleanup the next. Some of it is strategic. Some of it is unglamorous. Part of the job is building the templates and systems that make that work repeatable, so the role will likely look different in 6 months, and may be less GTM oriented then. We want someone who enjoys that variety, jumps into new problems as they come up, owns the outcome, and leaves each process better than they found it. The right person is analytical, commercially sharp, highly organized, and comfortable working with leadership, sales, finance, product, and engineering in the same day.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - You will put together pricing, proposals, customer business cases, and value models for complex deals, and support contract review. Over time, you will turn this work into templates and systems the sales team can run on their own.

 - You will build business cases for new markets and new products, and keep the team current on what competitors are doing.

 - You will help leadership and the sales team see the pipeline clearly through forecasting, CRM hygiene, and dashboards.

 - You will support planning, budgeting, and board and investor reporting, and track spend across the business, including production, R&D, SaaS, and vendor spend.

 - You will build processes, documentation, and decision frameworks where today there may only be spreadsheets, Slack threads, and ad hoc decisions.

 - You will handle the day-to-day work that keeps the business running: cleaning up data, coordinating vendors, chasing down numbers, and taking problems from "someone should figure this out" to a clear owner and outcome.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 5 years of experience in consulting, investment banking, or investing, or in business operations, revenue operations, or a similarly analytical role at an early-stage, high-growth startup.

 - Strong with spreadsheets and financial models, and comfortable in a CRM.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - Good judgment and the ability to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

 - A low-ego team player who takes on the detailed, behind-the-scenes work without being asked and improves it over time.

 - A builder mentality: you are excited to create the first version of a system and turn one-off work into something others can reuse.

 - A generalist who enjoys variety and is excited to take on whatever problem matters most, knowing the role will change as the company grows.

 - Comfortable working without much direction or full context. You find what you need, make a reasonable call, and flag what you assumed.

 - You use AI tools to improve systems and get more done, without handing your thinking to them.

 - Interest in physical AI, hard industries, critical infrastructure, defense, energy, or industrial technology and the ability and desire to get up to speed on technical products.

 - Based in San Francisco and excited to work in person.

title: Welding Sales Manager
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Fabricators across the country can't hire enough welders, and you know it better than most, because you've run a torch yourself. As our Welding Sales Manager, you'll show shops what cobot welding does for their throughput, quality, and people, and you'll own the national welding number. Welding is one of our fastest-growing applications, and you'll be the person who helps it grow even faster.


📍 Location

This role is remote within the United States, and we prefer candidates in NYC metro, North Carolina, California, Illinois or Texas. Expect to travel frequently to customer sites, regional teams, trade shows, and partners (~50% domestic travel).


What you'll do

- Own the welding number. You carry the national quota for welding systems and revenue across direct and partner sales. You build and manage the welding pipeline and forecast with each region, and you measure success by installed, producing systems, not just bookings.

- Partner with Regional Sales Managers. You co-sell welding opportunities with RSMs in every territory, from discovery through close. That means welding-specific discovery, part and joint reviews, and ROI conversations with fabricators. You'll join customer site visits, demos, and weld trials alongside our Welding Applications Engineers, and you'll raise the welding knowledge of the broader sales team through training, deal reviews, and ride-alongs.

- Sell direct MIG welding systems. You help shops evaluate cobot MIG welding against their part mix, volumes, and labor constraints, and you lead the proposals, pricing, and negotiation on welding deals.

- Build the partner channel. You recruit and manage gas and welding distributors as a lead source for Standard Bots welding. You also support partner-built solutions, such as laser welding cells, from the first conversation to repeatable sales.

- Be the voice of the welding customer. You bring field feedback on ease of use, features, and competitive gaps to the welding product team, and you represent Standard Bots at welding and fabrication trade shows and industry events.


What you'll bring

- Hands-on welding experience. You've laid beads and you know what a good weld looks like. MIG is required; TIG or laser is a plus.

- 5+ years in welding sales or welding applications, ideally robotic or automated welding.

- A track record of closing capital equipment deals with manufacturers and fabricators.

- Comfort working as an individual contributor who leads through influence across regional sales teams.

- Willingness to travel frequently to customer sites, trade shows, and partner meetings.


Nice to have

- Experience with a welding OEM, welding distributor, or robotic welding integrator.

- Existing relationships with gas and welding distributors.

- AWS certification (CW, CWI, or similar).

- Experience building or managing a channel partner program.


Compensation and Benefits

The on target earnings (OTE) range for this role is $190,000 - $225,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. title: Account Executive, Velocity Platforms (Hunter)
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Platform Sales team works with B2B Software Platforms to help them facilitate payments for their customers using our Stripe Connect product. Software Platforms, also known as B2B Indirect, are software platform businesses who serve other businesses. Platforms already using Stripe include Shopify, Lightspeed and Mindbody.
As a key member to the Stripe Platforms team, you will manage and elevate relationships with a named account list while identifying new growth opportunities and ways Stripe can exceed expectations.
What you’ll do
As an Account Executive (New Business), you will create partnerships between Stripe and the most innovative and fastest-growing software platforms in the world by helping them to understand how Stripe’s online commerce infrastructure can make payments a competitive advantage for their businesses.
Responsibilities
Directly manage and nurture a named account list and develop account plans for winning and expanding business with upper middle market and enterprise companies
Build and maintain key relationships with C-level executives, while orchestrating touchpoints with Stripe executives
Contribute to shaping our platform partnership strategy and building repeatable processes and scaled engagement models
Develop and execute outbound strategies to create and nurture opportunities
Own the full sales cycle from lead to close for Startup, SMB and mid-market platforms
Coordinate and support the implementation for sold platforms and ramp for their usage of Stripe products
Lead and contribute to team projects to develop and refine our sales process
Engage with Product and Engineering teams to help provide product feedback

You are an adept salesperson and relationship manager capable of engaging in business-level and technical conversations at multiple levels of the organization, including the CTO, COO, and CFO. You are used to building value in competitive situations and enjoy working on products that require deep product understanding, combined with technical knowledge. You are naturally analytical and enjoy digging into business models and helping customers quantify their investment decisions. You get excited about prospecting, and are capable of independently leading a sales cycle from start to finish. 2+ years of sales or prospecting experience, preferably at a technology company, with a track record of top performance
Ability to understand complex technical ecosystems and build great relationships with technical customers
Analytical ability to manage complex sales cycles, directly selling a technology product or service, preferably at an API-first company, with a record of top performance
Experience managing projects with input from cross-functional teams, including managing user deployments and ramp timelines
A knack for working well with a wide range of stakeholders, both internally and externally
Ability and motivation to operate in a highly ambiguous and fast-paced environment
Superior verbal and written communication skills
Proven ability to close deals, manage a full sales cycle and meet or exceed sales targets
Payments experience is preferred

description:

You'll join a diverse, experienced team with rapidly growing scope while working with one of the industry's most valuable autonomous vehicle datasets. In this role, you will:
